# LA Value Pro

> LA Value Pro (lavaluepro.com) provides certified desktop appraisals of single-family homes and condominiums across Los Angeles County, California, for date-of-death and step-up in basis, trust and estate administration, gift tax (Form 709), Prop 19 parent-child transfers, divorce and date-of-separation values, family sales, and other retrospective (past-date) valuations. Reports are prepared and signed by Brian Ward, California Certified Residential Real Estate Appraiser (license AR036053), who has appraised Southern California homes since 2004.

## Key facts
- Service: desktop residential appraisal (no site visit; public records, MLS data, client photos, comparable sales analysis under USPAP)
- Properties: single-family homes and condominiums only (not 2–4 units, land, commercial, or mixed-use)
- Coverage: 144 cities and communities in Los Angeles County; predominantly rural areas (unincorporated Antelope Valley, Acton, Agua Dulce, Santa Monica Mountains canyons) are not covered
- Fees: Standard Desktop $449; Basic Desktop $299; same fee for current and past effective dates
- Turnaround: confirmation and invoice within one business day; report 5–7 business days after payment
- Ordering: online request form at https://lavaluepro.com/order; email contact@lavaluepro.com
- Appraiser: Brian Ward, California Certified Residential Real Estate Appraiser, license AR036053 (California Bureau of Real Estate Appraisers)
- Related: LA Value Pro is the Los Angeles County service of Brian Ward Appraisal (https://www.brianward.com); statewide desktop date-of-death appraisals at https://date-of-death.com/
- Not provided: legal or tax advice

## Report tiers
- Standard Desktop: $449 per property. Best for CPA files, trusts with several beneficiaries, gift tax returns, and any value that may be reviewed later.
- Basic Desktop: $299 per property. Best for Simpler estates and family decisions where a concise, fully supported value is enough.

## Appraisal services
- [Date-of-Death Appraisals](https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/date-of-death): The fair market value of a home on the day its owner died, for basis records, trust accounting, and estate files.
- [Step-Up in Basis Appraisals](https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/step-up-in-basis): Documents the new tax basis of an inherited home so capital gains or rental depreciation are calculated correctly.
- [Trust Administration Appraisals](https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/trust-administration): A neutral value for successor trustees who must account to beneficiaries, distribute property, or arrange a buyout.
- [Estate Settlement & Estate Tax Appraisals](https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/estate-settlement): Values for executors and administrators settling an estate, filing Form 706, or deciding whether to sell or distribute a home.
- [Gift Tax Appraisals](https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/gift-tax): Fair market value on the date a home or an interest in one is given, prepared for Form 709 reporting.
- [Prop 19 Parent-Child Transfer Appraisals](https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/prop-19): Checks the market value that drives the Prop 19 property tax calculation when a parent's home passes to a child.
- [Divorce & Date-of-Separation Appraisals](https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/divorce): A neutral market value of the family home, current or as of the date of separation, for settlement and buyouts.
- [Family Sale & Co-Owner Buyout Appraisals](https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/family-sale): Fair market value for sales between relatives, sibling buyouts of inherited homes, and dividing co-owned property.
- [Retrospective Appraisals](https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/retrospective): Value as of any past date: a gift, a transfer into a trust, a date of separation, or the start of a tax year.

- [Malibu](https://lavaluepro.com/areas/malibu): Coastal city of beachfront strands, bluff-top estates and canyon homes
- [Brentwood](https://lavaluepro.com/areas/brentwood): Canyon estates, Brentwood Park's broad lots and small-lot Brentwood Glen houses
- [Pacific Palisades](https://lavaluepro.com/areas/pacific-palisades): Bluff-top and canyon neighborhoods above the Pacific, rebuilding after the 2025 fire
- [Bel Air](https://lavaluepro.com/areas/bel-air): Gated estate lots and winding hillside streets climbing toward Mulholland Drive
- [Westwood](https://lavaluepro.com/areas/westwood): Janss-era homes, UCLA housing and the Wilshire Corridor's condominium towers
- [West Los Angeles](https://lavaluepro.com/areas/west-los-angeles): Sawtelle multifamily blocks and Rancho Park's 1920s single-family streets
- [Cheviot Hills](https://lavaluepro.com/areas/cheviot-hills): Rolling 1920s tracts beside the Rancho Park and Hillcrest golf courses

- [Mar Vista](https://lavaluepro.com/areas/mar-vista): Postwar houses north of Venice Boulevard, apartment blocks to the south
- [Palms](https://lavaluepro.com/areas/palms): Dense apartment district with Westside Village's 1939 tract houses
- [Playa del Rey](https://lavaluepro.com/areas/playa-del-rey): Bluff-top view homes above the beach, lagoon-side condominiums below
- [Playa Vista](https://lavaluepro.com/areas/playa-vista): Planned community of condominiums and townhomes on the former Hughes Aircraft site
- [Westchester](https://lavaluepro.com/areas/westchester): Late-1930s and postwar tract houses between LAX and the Ballona bluffs
- [Marina del Rey](https://lavaluepro.com/areas/marina-del-rey): County harbor of high-rise condominiums and apartments on long-term ground leases

# Full reference text

## Frequently asked questions

Q: What is a desktop appraisal?
A: A desktop appraisal is a full appraisal analysis prepared without a visit to the property. The appraiser relies on public records, multiple listing service data, prior listing information, and photos and details the client supplies, then analyzes comparable sales and reaches a reasoned opinion of value under USPAP.

Q: Will the IRS accept a desktop appraisal?
A: Federal tax rules call for a well-supported fair market value; they do not require that the appraiser inspect the interior. Certified desktop reports are widely used to document date-of-death values and stepped-up basis. Your CPA decides what support your particular return needs.

Q: Which properties do you appraise?
A: Single-family homes and condominiums, including townhome-style condos, in our Los Angeles County coverage area. We do not take 2–4 unit buildings, vacant land, commercial or mixed-use property, or homes under construction. If you are unsure, send the request and we will tell you.

Q: Which parts of Los Angeles County do you cover?
A: 144 cities and communities, from Malibu and the South Bay to Pasadena, Pomona, Santa Clarita, Lancaster, Long Beach, and Avalon. We do not cover the county's predominantly rural areas or its largely industrial cities, where desktop analysis is less reliable.

Q: How much does an appraisal cost?
A: $299 for a Basic Desktop report and $449 for a Standard Desktop report, per property. The fee is the same for current and past effective dates and is confirmed before you pay.

Q: What is the difference between Basic and Standard?
A: Both use the same research and comparable sales analysis and reach a fully supported value. The Standard report adds a location map, comparable sale photos, a market conditions analysis, and a fuller written explanation, which CPAs and trusts with several beneficiaries usually prefer.

Q: How long does it take?
A: We reply with a confirmation and invoice within one business day of your request. The signed report is typically delivered 5–7 business days after payment.

Q: Can you appraise a home as of a date in the past?
A: Yes. Retrospective values as of a date of death, a gift, a transfer, or a date of separation are routine, and they cost the same as a current-value report.

Q: Do you need to go inside the home?
A: No. That is what makes a desktop report practical for estates: nobody has to schedule access to a vacant house or coordinate with family members who live there. We do ask for photos.

Q: What if the home has changed since the date of death?
A: Tell us what changed and when. The report describes the property as it was on the effective date, so older photos, prior listing photos, and plain descriptions all help.

Q: Who prepares the appraisal?
A: Brian Ward, a California Certified Residential Real Estate Appraiser (license AR036053) who has appraised Southern California homes since 2004. Every report is researched, written, and signed by him.

Q: How do I pay?
A: After we confirm your request, we email a secure online invoice. Work begins when it is paid.

Q: Is LA Value Pro connected to date-of-death.com?
A: Yes. LA Value Pro is the Los Angeles County service of Brian Ward Appraisal, which also operates the statewide date-of-death.com service and brianward.com. Same appraiser, same standards.

Q: Do you give legal or tax advice?
A: No. We provide the appraisal. Questions about elections, filing deadlines, Prop 19 eligibility, or how a value is reported belong with your attorney or CPA.

Q: Can I order appraisals for several properties at once?
A: Yes. List every address in one request and we will confirm each property and quote them together.

## Date-of-Death Appraisals (https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/date-of-death)
A date-of-death appraisal establishes what a home was worth on the day its owner died. For inherited Los Angeles County property, that figure becomes the heirs' new tax basis, anchors trust and estate accounting, and gives everyone involved a neutral number to work from, even when the appraisal is ordered months or years later.

### Why the date matters more than today's price
Federal tax law resets the basis of inherited property to its fair market value on the date of death (Internal Revenue Code §1014). If a parent bought a Pasadena bungalow decades ago, the heirs' gain on a later sale is measured from the date-of-death value, not the original purchase price. A credible retrospective appraisal is how that number is documented.
Because the valuation looks backward, the analysis relies on comparable sales and market conditions that existed at the time, not on current listings. In a market that has moved quickly, the gap between a date-of-death value and today's value can be large in either direction.
### Ordering one long after the fact
Many trustees and heirs first learn they need a date-of-death value when a CPA prepares a return or when the house is about to be sold. That is common and not a problem: a retrospective appraisal can be prepared for any past date for which sales data exists, and Los Angeles County's sales record runs deep.
### California community property and a full step-up
When a married couple holds a home as community property, both halves generally receive a new basis at the first spouse's death, not only the decedent's half (IRC §1014(b)(6)). That makes the date-of-death value of a California home doubly important for a surviving spouse. Your CPA or estate attorney will confirm how title was held and how the rule applies to you.
### What the report documents
Each report states the effective date, describes the property as of that date, presents the comparable sales relied on and the market conditions at the time, and explains the reasoning behind the final opinion of fair market value. It is prepared under the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP) and signed by a California Certified Residential Real Estate Appraiser, which is the support CPAs and estate attorneys expect to find in the file.

Q: Can the appraisal use photos taken after the date of death?
A: Yes. Recent photos help us understand the home. Tell us about anything that changed after the date of death, such as cleanup, repairs, or remodeling, so the report reflects the property as it was on the effective date.

Q: Is a date-of-death appraisal the same as the probate referee's value?
A: No. In a California probate, a court-appointed probate referee values real property for the estate inventory. Heirs and trustees often still want an independent date-of-death appraisal for income-tax basis records, trust administration, or decisions among family members; your attorney can advise how the two fit together.

Q: What if the home sold shortly after the death?
A: A nearby-in-time, arm's-length sale of the home itself is meaningful evidence. The appraisal still analyzes the market as of the date of death and explains how the later sale relates to that value.

## Step-Up in Basis Appraisals (https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/step-up-in-basis)
When real estate passes to heirs at death, its tax basis generally steps up to fair market value on the date of death. A step-up in basis appraisal documents that value so heirs can calculate capital gains when they sell, or depreciation if they keep the home as a rental, on firm ground.

### How the step-up works, in one example
Suppose a Lakewood house bought for $40,000 in 1972 was worth $850,000 when its owner died, and the heirs later sell it for $870,000. Measured from the stepped-up basis, the taxable gain is roughly $20,000 before selling costs. Measured from the 1972 price, it would be about $830,000. The numbers are hypothetical, but the gap shows why the date-of-death value deserves careful support.
### Inherited and gifted property are treated differently
Property given away during the owner's life usually keeps the giver's original basis (IRC §1015), so a home deeded to a child before death can carry a much larger built-in gain than the same home inherited. If a transfer happened shortly before a death, or if you are unsure whether a deed counted as a gift, ask your tax adviser before relying on a step-up.
### Keeping the home as a rental
Heirs who rent out an inherited house or condo depreciate the building, not the land, starting from the stepped-up basis. If you plan to rent the property, mention it in your request and ask about including an opinion of site value, which your tax preparer can use to separate land from improvements.
### Support that stands up later
Basis questions tend to surface years afterward, when the property is sold and a return is reviewed. A report signed by a certified appraiser, built on sales from the right period and kept in the estate or tax file, answers those questions without anyone having to reconstruct the market from memory.

Q: Do both spouses' halves step up in California?
A: Often, yes. For community property, IRC §1014(b)(6) generally allows both halves to receive a new basis at the first spouse's death. How title was held matters, so confirm with your CPA or attorney.

Q: Is there a deadline for a step-up appraisal?
A: There is no fixed deadline, but the value must be supported when the sale or depreciation is reported. Retrospective reports can be prepared years later; ordering sooner simply makes records easier to gather.

Q: Does the alternate valuation date apply to us?
A: Only estates that file a federal estate tax return (Form 706) can elect it, and only when the election lowers both the gross estate and the tax. Your CPA will say whether the report should use the date of death or the date six months later.

## Trust Administration Appraisals (https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/trust-administration)
Successor trustees use an independent appraisal to value trust real estate at the settlor's death, divide property fairly among beneficiaries, document distributions, and support a buyout when one beneficiary keeps the house. A certified desktop report gives the trustee a defensible number without scheduling an inspection of a home that may be vacant or occupied by family.

### A neutral number for a fiduciary
A trustee owes beneficiaries impartial treatment and accurate accountings. Relying on a broker's opinion or an online estimate invites second-guessing, especially when one beneficiary is buying out the others. An appraisal by a state-certified appraiser who has no stake in the outcome gives the trustee documentation that is easy to explain.
### Equal shares, buyouts, and in-kind distributions
When one sibling keeps the family home and the others receive cash or other assets, the home's value sets the size of every share. The same is true when properties are distributed in kind. We can value the property as of the date of death for tax purposes and, if the distribution happens much later, as of a current date as well.
### Several properties, one request
Trusts in Los Angeles County often hold more than one property, such as a family home and a condo, or a house in the Valley and another in the South Bay. List each address in a single request and we will quote them together.
### Working alongside the trust's advisers
Reports are addressed to the client who orders them and can name the trust's attorney and CPA as intended users so the same report serves accounting, tax basis, and distribution decisions.

Q: Who usually orders the appraisal, the trustee or a beneficiary?
A: Most often the trustee, as part of administering the trust. A beneficiary can also order one; tell us who will rely on the report so it names the right intended users.

Q: Can one report serve both tax and distribution purposes?
A: Frequently, yes, when both rely on the date-of-death value. If the distribution occurs well after the death, a second effective date may be needed; we will flag that when we review your request.

Q: What if the beneficiaries disagree about value?
A: A neutral report is often the starting point that resolves the disagreement. If you expect the value to be contested in court, ask us before ordering whether a desktop report is the right fit.

## Estate Settlement & Estate Tax Appraisals (https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/estate-settlement)
Executors and administrators need a supported value for Los Angeles County real estate when settling an estate, preparing a federal estate tax return, or deciding whether to sell or distribute a home. A certified desktop appraisal documents fair market value as of the date of death, or as of the alternate valuation date when the estate elects it.

### Federal estate tax returns
Only larger estates must file Form 706, but those that do report real property at fair market value, and the IRS looks for appraisal support. When an estate elects the alternate valuation date, the report can value the property as of that date instead. For estates that file, the beneficiaries' income-tax basis must generally be consistent with the value reported for estate tax (IRC §1014(f)), so the appraisal effectively serves both purposes.
### Probate and the referee's inventory
In a California probate, real property in the inventory is valued by a court-appointed probate referee. An independent appraisal still has a place: it supports income-tax basis records, helps the personal representative and heirs decide whether to sell or distribute, and gives everyone a second, independent view of the market.
### Deciding whether to sell
When an estate plans to sell, the executor needs a realistic expectation of what the property will bring, and heirs want assurance that it is not being sold short. A current-value report, ordered alongside or after a date-of-death report, gives that context.

Q: Does every estate need a Form 706 appraisal?
A: No. Most estates fall below the federal filing threshold. Even then, a date-of-death value is usually needed to establish the heirs' basis for a later sale.

Q: Can you value the property as of the alternate valuation date?
A: Yes. Give us both dates if the estate has not decided; we can discuss whether one report or two is appropriate.

Q: Do you provide legal or tax advice?
A: No. We provide the appraisal. Questions about elections, filing requirements, and how a value is reported belong with your estate attorney or CPA.

## Gift Tax Appraisals (https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/gift-tax)
Giving a home, or a share of one, to a family member is a gift of its fair market value. A gift tax appraisal documents that value as of the date of the gift for the federal gift tax return (Form 709), and a report that meets the IRS's appraisal requirements helps establish the adequate disclosure that starts the limitations period on the gift.

### What the IRS looks for
Treasury Regulation §301.6501(c)-1(f)(3) describes an appraisal that can satisfy adequate disclosure on a gift tax return: prepared by a qualified appraiser, stating the valuation date and purpose, describing the property, and explaining the method and comparable evidence. Our reports are written with that list in mind; your CPA decides how the report is attached and disclosed.
### Gifts of a partial interest
Parents often add a child to title or give a percentage interest in a home. The report values the whole property; any discount for a fractional interest is a separate, specialized analysis that your tax adviser may request from a business valuation professional.
### Gifted homes keep the giver's basis
Unlike inherited property, a home received as a gift during the giver's life generally carries over the giver's original tax basis. Families weighing a lifetime gift against an inheritance often compare the two outcomes with their CPA; a current-value appraisal supplies the market side of that comparison.

Q: What date should the appraisal use?
A: The date the gift was complete, which for real estate is usually the date the deed was delivered or recorded. Your attorney or CPA can confirm the right date.

Q: Can you value a gift made in a prior year?
A: Yes. Gift appraisals are frequently retrospective because the return is prepared after the year ends.

Q: Does a sale to a child below market count as a gift?
A: The difference between the price paid and fair market value is generally treated as a gift. See family sale appraisals for how we document value in those transactions.

## Prop 19 Parent-Child Transfer Appraisals (https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/prop-19)
Since February 16, 2021, Proposition 19 has narrowed California's parent-to-child property tax exclusion. Whether a transferred Los Angeles County home keeps part of its old assessed value now depends on how the home's market value at the transfer compares with the parent's taxable value plus an exclusion amount, so the market value itself carries real tax consequences.

### How the calculation works
If the child qualifies, the new taxable value is the parent's factored base year value, plus any amount by which the home's market value exceeds that base value plus the exclusion amount. The exclusion amount started at $1 million and is adjusted for inflation every two years.
A hypothetical: a Torrance home with a factored base year value of $150,000 and a market value of $1,600,000 at transfer. Using a round $1 million exclusion for illustration, the excess is $1,600,000 minus $1,150,000, or $450,000, so the new taxable value would be about $600,000 rather than $1,600,000. A different market value changes that result dollar for dollar.
### Where an independent appraisal helps
The Los Angeles County Assessor determines market value at the transfer. An independent appraisal lets the family check that figure, and if it looks high, the report is evidence you can bring to an informal review or an appeal before the Assessment Appeals Board. Families also use appraisals before a transfer, to see whether a child moving in is likely to preserve meaningful tax savings.
### The transfer date
For a transfer at death, the change in ownership generally occurs on the date of death, so the same effective date often serves the step-up in basis and the Prop 19 calculation. For lifetime transfers, the date is tied to the deed.
### Know what an appraiser does and does not do
We appraise fair market value. Eligibility, filing deadlines, and claim forms (the parent-child claim is BOE-19-P) are matters for the Assessor's office and your attorney; we are glad to coordinate with them.

Q: Does the Assessor have to accept a private appraisal?
A: No. The Assessor makes its own determination. An appraisal is evidence you can present if you request a review or file an assessment appeal.

Q: Can the same report support step-up in basis?
A: Often, yes, when the transfer occurred at death and both purposes use the date-of-death value. Tell us both purposes when you order.

Q: Does Prop 19 apply to rentals passed to children?
A: Prop 19's parent-child exclusion is limited to the family home and qualifying family farms, so other property is generally reassessed at market value. Confirm your situation with the Assessor or an attorney.

## Divorce & Date-of-Separation Appraisals (https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/divorce)
Dividing a Los Angeles County home in a divorce starts with a value both sides can accept. A desktop appraisal gives spouses, their attorneys, or a mediator a neutral, documented market value as of today, as of the date of separation, or both.

### Current value or date of separation
California Family Code §2552 generally values community assets as near as practicable to the time of trial, but the court can use another date for good cause, and settlement talks frequently reference the date of separation. When the right date is unsettled, a report with both values lets everyone see the difference before negotiating.
### Built for a buyout
When one spouse keeps the home, the buyout figure depends on the market value less what is owed against the property. A neutral appraisal removes the most argued-over number from the conversation.
### Neutral by design
We do not advocate for either side. When both spouses agree to share one appraiser, the report can name both as intended users, which often saves the cost and delay of dueling valuations.
### When a desktop report fits
Desktop appraisals work well for mediation, settlement negotiations, and agreed buyouts. If the value is likely to be litigated, or the home has significant condition issues, tell us before ordering so we can discuss whether an inspection-based assignment is a better choice.

Q: Can both spouses use the same appraisal?
A: Yes. A jointly ordered report can name both parties and their attorneys as intended users.

Q: Do you need access to the house?
A: No. The analysis uses public records, sales data, and photos the parties provide. Either spouse can supply photos; it helps when both agree on them.

Q: Can you value the home as of a past date of separation?
A: Yes. Retrospective values are routine in family law matters.

## Family Sale & Co-Owner Buyout Appraisals (https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/family-sale)
Selling a home to a relative, buying out a sibling's share of an inherited house, or dividing property held with a partner all go more smoothly with an independent value. A desktop appraisal documents fair market value so the price can be defended to the IRS, to other family members, and to the county assessor.

### Selling below market is partly a gift
When a parent sells a home to a child for less than it is worth, the difference is generally treated as a gift for federal tax purposes and may need to be reported on Form 709. An appraisal fixes the market value so everyone knows how much of the transaction is a sale and how much is a gift.
### Buying out co-heirs
Inherited homes are often owned by several siblings, and one of them wants to keep the house. The appraisal sets the starting point for each share, and because it comes from a neutral, licensed professional, it tends to settle the question of price rather than reopen it.
### Private sales without agents
A sale between people who know each other skips the market exposure that normally tests a price. An appraisal replaces that test with documented comparable sales, which is useful for the buyer, the seller, and anyone who later reviews the transaction.
### Property tax considerations
Transfers between parents and children, by sale or gift, can raise Proposition 19 questions about reassessment. See our Prop 19 page for how market value enters that calculation.

Q: Can both the buyer and seller rely on the report?
A: Yes. Name both when you order, and the report will identify them as intended users.

Q: Is a desktop appraisal enough for a family sale?
A: For most single-family homes and condominiums with typical condition, yes. If the property has major unpermitted work or damage, tell us first.

Q: Can you value the home as of the date the siblings inherited it?
A: Yes. Many buyouts use both the date-of-death value and a current value; we can provide either or both.

## Retrospective Appraisals (https://lavaluepro.com/appraisals/retrospective)
A retrospective appraisal values a property as of a specific date in the past: the date of a death or gift, a transfer into or out of a trust, a date of separation, or the start of a tax year. Los Angeles County's long, detailed record of closed sales makes it possible to reconstruct values for dates years back.

### How a past market is reconstructed
We study sales that closed in the months around the effective date, the listings and pending sales that existed then, and the direction the market was moving. Adjustments reflect the market as buyers saw it at that time. Nothing that happened after the effective date, such as a later boom or decline, is allowed to influence the value.
### Describing the property as it was
If the home has been remodeled, repaired, or damaged since the effective date, the report should describe it as it existed then. Old photos, prior listing photos, permits, and plain descriptions from family members all help.
### Large events and dividing lines
Some dates fall on the other side of a major event: a rate shock, a market turn, or the January 2025 fires in the Palisades and Altadena. For those assignments, comparable selection is anchored firmly to the effective date, and the report explains why later sales were set aside.

Q: How far back can you appraise?
A: Many years, as long as reliable sales data from the period exists. Tell us the date and we will confirm before you pay.

Q: Does a retrospective appraisal cost more?
A: No. Our fees are the same for current and past effective dates.

Q: Can one report contain two dates?
A: When two dates are needed, such as date of death and a current value, we will tell you whether one report or two is the cleaner approach.

## What photos to send for a desktop appraisal (https://lavaluepro.com/guides/photos-for-a-desktop-appraisal)
A desktop appraisal is only as good as the information behind it. Public records and sales data describe the neighborhood well, but photos are how the appraiser sees the condition and quality of the home itself. This checklist covers what to send, in roughly the order to take it.
### Outside the home
The front of the house from the street, straight on; The street in both directions, showing neighboring homes; The back of the house and the yard; Any pool, spa, detached garage, guest house, or accessory dwelling unit; The roof if visible from the ground, and any obvious exterior damage; For condos: the building exterior, entry, parking, and common areas you can access;
### Inside the home
Every room, taken from a corner so most of the room is visible; The kitchen, including counters, cabinets, and appliances; Each bathroom, including the shower or tub and vanity; Flooring changes, built-ins, and any finished basement or attic space; The water heater, furnace or HVAC unit, and electrical panel; Any damage, unfinished work, leaks, or deferred maintenance;
Phone photos are fine. Turn on the lights and open the blinds; daylight makes condition easier to judge.
### Documents that help
Permits or plans for additions, garage conversions, or ADUs; A list of updates with approximate years (roof, kitchen, baths, windows, systems); For condos: the HOA name, monthly dues, and any special assessments; Any prior appraisal, inspection report, or listing information you have;
### When the value is for a past date
If the appraisal is for a date of death or another past date, the report describes the home as it was then. Recent photos still help, but also send anything that shows the earlier condition: old family photos, a prior listing, insurance photos, or a short description of what has changed since. Cleaning out a home or making repairs after a death is normal; just tell us what was done.
### How to send them
After the invoice is paid, we will email instructions for sharing photos. Send them as originals rather than screenshots so detail is preserved.

## Inheriting a home in Los Angeles County: the paperwork that usually follows (https://lavaluepro.com/guides/inheriting-a-home-in-los-angeles-county)
When a parent or spouse dies owning a home in Los Angeles County, the same handful of tasks comes up in most families. This overview lists them in a typical order so nothing important is missed. It is general information, not legal or tax advice; an estate attorney can tell you which steps apply to your situation.
### 1. Gather certified death certificates
Several offices and institutions will each want a certified copy. Funeral homes usually order them; additional copies are available from the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk.
### 2. Find out how the home was titled
The deed tells you what comes next. A home held in a living trust is administered by the successor trustee, usually without probate. Joint tenancy passes to the surviving owner. A home held in the decedent's name alone may require probate. An estate attorney can confirm the path.
### 3. Record the right affidavit, if one applies
When a trustee or joint tenant dies, an affidavit of death is commonly recorded with the Registrar-Recorder to document the change. A Preliminary Change of Ownership Report usually accompanies documents that are recorded.
### 4. Notify the Assessor
California requires a Change in Ownership Statement – Death of Real Property Owner (form BOE-502-D) to be filed with the county assessor, generally within 150 days of the date of death. The Los Angeles County Assessor publishes the form.
### 5. Consider Proposition 19
If a child will move into a parent's home, a parent-child exclusion claim may preserve part of the parent's assessed value. The rules are narrower than they were before 2021, and the market value at the transfer matters. See our Prop 19 page for how the calculation works.
### 6. Establish the date-of-death value
The home's fair market value on the date of death generally becomes the heirs' new tax basis. A date-of-death appraisal documents it for the trust or estate file and for the eventual sale.
### 7. Protect the property
Keep property taxes, utilities, and insurance current. Many homeowners policies limit coverage when a home sits vacant, so call the insurer if no one is living there.
### 8. Decide: keep, rent, or sell
Heirs often choose between a buyout, a sale, or keeping the home as a rental. Each choice benefits from a clear value; buyouts and in-kind distributions are covered on our trust administration and family sale pages.

## Desktop or traditional appraisal: which does your situation need? (https://lavaluepro.com/guides/desktop-vs-traditional-appraisal)
Both kinds of appraisal reach a reasoned opinion of market value under the same professional standards. The difference is how the appraiser learns about the property: from records, data, and photos, or from walking through it. For most estate and family matters involving ordinary single-family homes and condos, a desktop report gives the same answer faster and at lower cost.
### Side by side
Desktop appraisalTraditional appraisalProperty visitNoneInterior and exterior inspectionProperty informationPublic records, MLS history, client photos and detailsAppraiser's own measurements and observationsComparable sales analysisFullFullSchedulingNothing to scheduleAccess must be arrangedTypical fitBasis, trust accounting, gift returns, family negotiationsLitigation, unusual properties, significant condition questions
### When a desktop report is the right fit
The property is a single-family home or condominium in typical condition; The value is needed for tax basis, trust or estate accounting, a gift return, or a negotiated settlement; The home is vacant, out of reach, or occupied by someone who would rather not schedule a visit; The effective date is in the past, so today's interior tells only part of the story anyway;
### When to choose an inspection-based appraisal
The value is likely to be argued in court and testimony may be needed; The home is highly unusual, very large, or unlike anything nearby; There is major damage, extensive unpermitted construction, or a disputed condition; The property is a 2–4 unit building, vacant land, or mixed-use;
If any of these apply, tell us in your request. We would rather recommend the right kind of report than sell you the wrong one.

## Area notes

### Santa Monica (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/santa-monica)
Santa Monica is an incorporated beach city on Santa Monica Bay, bordered by Pacific Palisades, Brentwood, West Los Angeles, Mar Vista and Venice. Executors and trustees here often need a date-of-death value for a North of Montana house, a retrospective value for a converted condominium, or a buyout figure for a Sunset Park bungalow.
Housing: North of Montana Avenue the lots widen, and the blocks above San Vicente Boulevard hold the city's largest estate parcels. Between Wilshire and Montana, Craftsman houses and older duplexes sit among low-rise condominium buildings, while Ocean Park keeps early beach cottages near Main Street and Sunset Park is mostly single-family housing from the prewar and postwar decades. A notable share of the condominiums began as rental buildings converted under TORCA, a 1984 charter amendment that allowed tenant-approved conversions until 1996.
Appraisal considerations: The city has designated historic districts, including the Third Street Neighborhood and 11th Street Bungalow districts, so designation status should be confirmed before an older house is treated as land value. For TORCA conversions, remaining tenant occupancy and association reserves can affect marketability. Homes close to the airport may warrant a note on airport influence as of the effective date.
ZIP codes: 90401, 90402, 90403, 90404, 90405

### Beverly Hills (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/beverly-hills)
Incorporated in 1914, Beverly Hills is a separate city bordered by West Hollywood and by Los Angeles neighborhoods including Century City, Holmby Hills and the Beverly Hills Post Office area. Its housing runs from estates in the Flats to condominiums south of Wilshire Boulevard, and families and attorneys here commonly ask for date-of-death values for trust administration, divorce valuations of hillside residences, and Prop 19 analysis on transfers to children.
Housing: The Flats, between Santa Monica and Sunset boulevards, is a planned grid of wide, tree-lined streets with large lots holding period-revival and newer custom homes. North of Sunset the terrain turns to hillside, including Trousdale Estates, developed in the 1950s and 1960s on land that was once part of the Doheny estate and known for mid-century modern houses with city views. South of Wilshire the lots are smaller, and single-family streets sit beside the city's heaviest concentration of multifamily buildings, including condominiums.
Appraisal considerations: The city designates the area north of Sunset Boulevard a Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone, which brings brush-clearance duties and can affect insurability. Trousdale Estates has its own view-protection ordinance, and the city runs a permanent Mills Act program for designated landmarks. Comparable selection must also separate true Beverly Hills properties from Beverly Hills Post Office homes, which carry a 90210 address but lie in the City of Los Angeles.
ZIP codes: 90210, 90211, 90212

### West Hollywood (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/west-hollywood)
West Hollywood, incorporated in 1984, occupies a compact strip between Beverly Hills and Hollywood, with the Sunset Strip along its northern edge. Most of its housing is multifamily, so the questions we see usually involve condominium values for estates and trusts, date-of-separation values for a townhome, or the value of a single-family house in West Hollywood West or the Norma Triangle.
Housing: Apartment and condominium buildings dominate, including Spanish Revival and Art Deco apartment buildings from the 1920s concentrated around Fountain Avenue, Harper Avenue and Havenhurst Drive. Single-family houses are concentrated in West Hollywood West and the Norma Triangle, where many homes have been expanded or rebuilt. Condominiums range from converted older buildings to newer mid-rise projects, so building age can change sharply within a few blocks.
Appraisal considerations: The city's Rent Stabilization Ordinance covers much of the rental stock, which matters when a condominium is tenant-occupied on the effective date or when sales from converted buildings serve as comparables. Many period apartment buildings carry historic interest, so designation status should be checked for any property with redevelopment potential. Special assessments and reserve levels vary widely among older associations and belong in the condominium analysis.
ZIP codes: 90069, 90046, 90048

### Culver City (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/culver-city)
Culver City, incorporated in 1917, sits between Palms, Mar Vista, Baldwin Hills and Ladera Heights, with a downtown built around its film studios. Heirs and trustees here ask for date-of-death values on houses in Carlson Park or Sunkist Park, divorce valuations of hillside homes in Blair Hills or Culver Crest, and values for condominiums in the multifamily complexes of Fox Hills.
Housing: Most single-family streets carry modest prewar and postwar houses on standard city lots, many since enlarged or replaced. Blair Hills and Culver Crest are hillside neighborhoods with sloping lots, and many homes there have city views. Fox Hills, around Westfield Culver City, is made up largely of condominium and apartment complexes, and newer mixed-use buildings have been added near downtown and the E Line station.
Appraisal considerations: The city's eastern edge adjoins the Inglewood Oil Field; a settlement with the operator permits operations in the city's portion through 2029 with no new drilling, and the city's oil rules have changed more than once since 2023, so conditions as of the effective date matter and proximity to wells can be a location factor. Because Culver City is its own jurisdiction, ADU and lot-split permits follow Culver City rules rather than Los Angeles rules, which affects how added units and permitted area are verified.
ZIP codes: 90230, 90232, 90066

### Malibu (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/malibu)
Malibu, incorporated in 1991, is a long coastal city along Pacific Coast Highway west of Topanga and Pacific Palisades. Fire history shapes much of the valuation work here: families and attorneys ask for pre-fire values of homes lost in January 2025, land values for burned parcels, and date-of-death values that must reflect the market on one specific day.
Housing: Housing runs from beachfront strands such as Carbon Beach, Malibu Colony and Malibu Road to terrace and bluff neighborhoods like Point Dume and Malibu Park, and on into canyon and hillside homes reached by narrow, winding roads. Lot sizes range from narrow beach parcels to acreage in the western canyons, and most houses are custom builds of widely varying age and quality. Condominiums and townhomes make up only a small part of the stock.
Appraisal considerations: The 2025 Palisades Fire hit eastern Malibu hardest, with the city naming Big Rock, Carbon Mesa and La Costa among the worst-affected areas, while the 2018 Woolsey Fire destroyed hundreds of homes in western neighborhoods such as Malibu Park. Market conditions before and after each fire must be measured separately, and burned parcels are valued as land with attention to rebuild eligibility under state and city rules that allow like-for-like replacement with limited expansion. Septic capacity, geology and coastal permits also limit what many lots can support.
ZIP codes: 90265

### Brentwood (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/brentwood)
Brentwood is a City of Los Angeles community on the Westside, running from the flats south of Sunset Boulevard up through the canyons toward Mulholland Drive, between Pacific Palisades and the 405 Freeway. Trustees and families here typically need date-of-death values for estate-sized lots in Brentwood Park, retrospective values for canyon homes, and values for condominiums and townhomes in the flats near San Vicente Boulevard.
Housing: Brentwood Park, bordered by Oakmont, San Vicente, Allenford and Cliffwood, is a district of large estate lots, while Brentwood Glen, between Sunset, the 405 and the Veterans Affairs campus, has much smaller lots. North of Sunset, Kenter, Mandeville and Sullivan canyons hold hillside and canyon-floor homes, including equestrian properties in Sullivan Canyon. Crestwood Hills began in the late 1940s as a cooperative tract known for A. Quincy Jones modern houses, though the 1961 fire and decades of rebuilding changed much of its original character. South of Sunset, older houses share the streets with condominium and townhome buildings.
Appraisal considerations: Brentwood's hillside areas lie in a Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone; the 1961 Bel Air–Brentwood fire and the 2019 Getty Fire destroyed homes here, and the January 2025 Palisades Fire reached Mandeville Canyon, where at least one home burned, and forced evacuations. For effective dates in early 2025, we check whether nearby sales reflected disrupted post-fire conditions, and insurance availability can bear on canyon properties. Hillside lots fall under the City's Baseline Hillside Ordinance, so buildable floor area and access should be confirmed rather than assumed.
ZIP codes: 90049

### Pacific Palisades (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/pacific-palisades)
Pacific Palisades is a coastal community in the City of Los Angeles between Santa Monica and Malibu, founded in the early 1920s by a Methodist organization and spread across bluffs, mesas and canyons above Pacific Coast Highway. Since the January 2025 Palisades Fire, most requests we receive here involve pre-fire values of homes that were lost, land values for burned lots, and date-of-death values that must fall on the correct side of January 7, 2025.
Housing: The Alphabet Streets north of the Village were the first area built and have the smallest lots, while Marquez Knolls, the El Medio Bluffs and the Palisades Highlands spread across hillsides with ocean or canyon views. Huntington Palisades and the Riviera, near the Riviera Country Club, hold larger lots and custom estates, and Castellammare sits on steep slopes just above Pacific Coast Highway. Rustic Canyon and Temescal Canyon add wooded canyon-floor settings, and the Highlands contain separately named tracts such as The Summit and Country Estates.
Appraisal considerations: The Palisades Fire began on January 7, 2025, and destroyed large parts of the community, including much of the Alphabet Streets and Marquez Knolls, so an effective date before that day calls for pre-fire sales and conditions, and a later date for post-fire evidence. Burned parcels are valued as land, considering lot size, views, debris-removal status and rebuild rules; a 2025 state executive order and city action restricted SB 9 lot splits and duplexes in the burn area, so that potential should not be assumed. Fire-scarred slopes can also raise debris-flow and drainage concerns that buyers take into account.
ZIP codes: 90272

### Bel Air (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/bel-air)
Bel Air is a hillside community in the City of Los Angeles north of Sunset Boulevard, founded in 1923 by Alphonzo Bell and planned around large residential lots in the Santa Monica Mountains. Valuation requests here usually involve estate properties held in trust, date-of-death values for heirs settling a family residence, and divorce valuations in which land value and improvements must be analyzed separately.
Housing: The original Bel Air Estates subdivision and the streets inside the East Gate hold the oldest and often largest estates. Beyond the gates, the community extends north along canyon roads such as Stone Canyon Road and Roscomare Road, with lots ranging from level pads to steep slopes. Houses from the community's early decades stand beside mid-century homes and recent large-scale rebuilds. Detached single-family homes dominate the housing stock.
Appraisal considerations: Bel Air's hillsides fall within a Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone, and the community lost hundreds of homes in the 1961 fire and several more in a 2017 brush fire, so brush clearance, fire access and insurance terms deserve attention. Hillside lots are governed by the City's Baseline Hillside Ordinance, which limits floor area and grading, so the size of home a lot could support should be confirmed before land value is concluded. On large estates, adjustments for lot area and amenities should be supported by sales of comparable scale rather than by smaller homes nearby.
ZIP codes: 90077

### Westwood (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/westwood)
Westwood is the City of Los Angeles community surrounding UCLA, bounded roughly by Sunset Boulevard, Beverly Hills, Santa Monica Boulevard and the 405 Freeway. Requests here range from date-of-death values for condominiums on the Wilshire Corridor to trust valuations of single-family homes in Westwood Hills and Holmby Westwood and family-sale values for units near campus.
Housing: Development began in the early 1920s, when the Janss Investment Company began selling lots on the former Wolfskill Ranch, and the single-family streets still carry many homes from those first decades alongside later remodels and replacements. The Wilshire Corridor east of Westwood Boulevard is lined with condominium towers, a concentration of high-rise ownership housing unusual on the Westside. North Westwood Village is mainly multifamily housing near campus, and other blocks mix single-family homes with duplexes, apartments and condominiums.
Appraisal considerations: Wilshire Corridor units call for comparables from the same or similar towers, with adjustments for floor level, views, parking, building age and amenities, plus a review of reserves, special assessments and any building-wide repairs pending on the effective date. Single-family homes are often valued substantially for land, so lot dimensions and the floor-area limits of the City's Baseline Mansionization Ordinance matter. Near campus, homes with a long student-rental history may show deferred maintenance that comparables from owner-occupied blocks do not.
ZIP codes: 90024, 90025

### West Los Angeles (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/west-los-angeles)
West Los Angeles is a City of Los Angeles community between Santa Monica and Westwood, centered on the former city of Sawtelle, which joined Los Angeles in 1922. Heirs and trustees here commonly need values for townhomes and condominiums near Sawtelle Boulevard, date-of-death values for single-family homes in Rancho Park, and co-owner buyout values for houses held by siblings.
Housing: Sawtelle is among the most densely built parts of the Westside, where many older single-family lots have been replaced over the decades by apartment, condominium and small-lot townhome projects. South of Olympic Boulevard, Rancho Park was built out from the 1920s with Spanish Colonial bungalows and later ranch houses, and Westwood Gardens was developed in the mid-1940s and sold largely to returning veterans. Many original houses in these tracts have been expanded or replaced with larger new homes.
Appraisal considerations: Small-lot subdivision homes and townhomes are common here and should be compared with the same product type, since shared driveways, limited yards and the presence or absence of an association change how buyers value them. Homes near the 405 and 10 freeways can be affected by noise and traffic, so proximity is weighed with paired sales where the data allows. In Rancho Park and Westwood Gardens, original houses on standard lots are frequently bought for expansion or replacement, making land value a useful check.
ZIP codes: 90025, 90064

### Cheviot Hills (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/cheviot-hills)
Cheviot Hills is a residential City of Los Angeles neighborhood south of Century City, set on low hills between Rancho Park Golf Course, Hillcrest Country Club and the Exposition Boulevard corridor. Typical requests involve trust and estate values for long-held family homes, Prop 19 parent-to-child transfers, and divorce valuations where a recent remodel or rebuild must be weighed against older houses nearby.
Housing: Frans Nelson & Sons opened the original Cheviot Hills tract in 1923 on streets with Scottish names such as Glenbarr, Haddington and Bannockburn, with lots averaging roughly 65 by 140 feet. Country Club Highlands and Monte-Mar Vista date from 1923 and 1925, Cheviot Knolls from 1938, and California Country Club Estates, known as New Cheviot, from the early 1950s. The architecture runs from 1920s houses to mid-century designs by Raphael Soriano, Craig Ellwood and A. Quincy Jones, and many original homes have been replaced by larger new construction.
Appraisal considerations: Golf-course frontage and elevated lots with city views can carry premiums that should be measured from local sales, while lots on Motor Avenue or near the E Line tracks along the southern edge should be tested against interior-street sales. Flat lots fall under the City's Baseline Mansionization Ordinance and hillside lots under the Baseline Hillside Ordinance, which cap the size of a replacement home and so affect land value. Houses by recognized mid-century architects can carry added value, so design history should be researched before a home is treated as a teardown.
ZIP codes: 90064

### Venice (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/venice)
Venice was founded by Abbot Kinney in 1905 as a seaside resort and joined the City of Los Angeles in 1926; it now runs from the beach inland past Lincoln Boulevard between Santa Monica and Marina del Rey. Families and attorneys here bring us estate values for canal and walk-street homes, divorce valuations of remodeled bungalows, and retrospective values for condominiums near the sand.
Housing: Lots are generally small, and the housing mixes early 1900s cottages and bungalows, older multifamily buildings near Pacific Avenue, and many modern replacement houses. The Venice Canals hold houses fronting the waterways, while inland walk streets such as Nowita, Amoroso and Marco places line up homes facing pedestrian-only paths, with car access from rear alleys. Silver Strand and the Marina Peninsula hold houses and condominiums on narrow parcels close to the beach. Oakwood, Milwood and the Oxford Triangle add older single-family and small multifamily streets farther inland.
Appraisal considerations: Venice lies in the coastal zone and is governed by the Venice Coastal Zone Specific Plan, so additions, rebuilds and new units can require coastal development permits, which shapes what a buyer can do with an older house. The Venice Canal Historic District is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, and canal frontage, walk-street frontage and blocks closest to the beach each call for comparables from the same setting. Units in older multifamily buildings may fall under the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance, which affects value when a property is tenant-occupied.
ZIP codes: 90291, 90292

### Mar Vista (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/mar-vista)
Mar Vista is a City of Los Angeles community between Santa Monica, Venice, Palms and Culver City, first known as Ocean Park Heights and annexed in 1927. Typical requests involve date-of-death values for postwar houses held since they were new, co-owner buyouts among siblings, and values for condominiums and small multifamily properties south of Venice Boulevard.
Housing: North of Venice Boulevard the streets are mostly single-family houses built during the area's growth from the 1950s through the 1970s, originally modest homes on standard city lots. Many have been expanded or replaced, so original and rebuilt houses often stand side by side. The Gregory Ain Mar Vista Tract, built in 1948 with landscape design by Garrett Eckbo, is a cluster of modern houses that became the city's first post-World War II Historic Preservation Overlay Zone in 2003. South of Venice Boulevard the zoning shifts to apartments, including many dingbat buildings, along with condominium and townhome projects.
Appraisal considerations: Exterior changes in the Gregory Ain Mar Vista Tract go through HPOZ review, and buyers there may pay for original design, so tract homes should be compared with each other first. Homes near Santa Monica Airport warrant attention to airport influence as of the effective date, with the planned 2028 closure considered for later dates. Garage conversions and ADUs are common on standard lots and should be checked against permit records before they are counted as living area or rental units.
ZIP codes: 90066

### Palms (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/palms)
Palms dates to an 1886 tract map and joined the City of Los Angeles in 1915; it sits between Cheviot Hills, Mar Vista and Culver City and is crossed by Venice Boulevard, National Boulevard and Motor Avenue. Most requests we see here involve condominium and townhome values for estates and trusts, along with date-of-death and buyout values for the single-family houses of Westside Village.
Housing: Until the early 1960s Palms was mostly single-family houses with some duplexes and triplexes, many built in Craftsman and Spanish styles. The City then rezoned much of the district for large multifamily buildings, and most of the older houses gave way to apartments, with condominium and townhome buildings among them. Westside Village, laid out in 1939 by Fritz B. Burns, holds the main concentration of owner-occupied houses, originally small homes on lots of about 50 by 135 feet with single-car garages.
Appraisal considerations: Condominium comparables should come from buildings of similar age and size, with attention to parking, reserves and pending special assessments. Westside Village houses vary widely between original and expanded homes, and verifying permitted square footage, ADUs and garage conversions is essential before choosing comparables. Properties next to the freeways or the E Line right-of-way should be tested against interior-street sales.
ZIP codes: 90034

### Playa del Rey (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/playa-del-rey)
Playa del Rey is a coastal City of Los Angeles community bounded by Ballona Creek and Marina del Rey to the north, the Ballona Wetlands and Playa Vista to the northeast, Westchester to the east and LAX to the south. Requests here usually involve date-of-death values for bluff homes with ocean views, trust valuations of condominiums near the lagoon, and divorce valuations where view and noise factors must be weighed.
Housing: Lower Playa del Rey occupies low-lying ground that was once wetlands and dunes, with houses, apartments and condominiums near Culver Boulevard and Del Rey Lagoon, including the closely built 1956 apartment cluster locals call the Jungle. Above it, the Del Rey Hills, also called the Bluffs, rise along the coast with custom homes positioned for ocean views. The eastern part of the community is the most densely built, with apartment and condominium complexes. The original 1921 subdivision was Palisades del Rey, and its southern section, Surfridge, was cleared for LAX between 1966 and 1975.
Appraisal considerations: LAX lies directly south, so aircraft noise and flight-path position should be measured with paired sales rather than assumed. The community is in the coastal zone, and low-lying parcels near the lagoon and creek should be checked for flood-zone status. View premiums on the bluffs depend on how protected and how wide the view is, and condominium comparables should come from complexes with similar age, amenities and association costs.
ZIP codes: 90293

### Playa Vista (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/playa-vista)
Playa Vista is a master-planned community in the City of Los Angeles built since 2001 on the former Hughes Aircraft property, beneath the Westchester Bluffs and beside the Ballona Wetlands. Valuation requests here involve condominiums and townhomes held in trusts, date-of-separation values for homes bought new, and family transfers where association dues and community facilities must be considered.
Housing: Development began with the first phase in 2001 and continued with the later Village phase, producing a housing stock made up largely of condominiums, townhomes and apartments. Buildings date from the early 2000s onward, so age differences are smaller than in older neighborhoods, but floor plans, building types and locations within the community vary considerably. Residential blocks share the community with offices, retail at Runway and the tech campuses that have made the area part of Silicon Beach.
Appraisal considerations: Owners pay dues to the Playa Vista Parks and Landscape Corporation, which operates shared facilities such as The Resort and The CenterPointe Club, and condominium buildings carry their own association dues as well, so total monthly obligations belong in the analysis. Because of documented methane in the area, the City required membrane barriers, venting and alarms beneath buildings, and buyers may ask about these systems. Comparables are best drawn from the same phase and product type, since a townhome and a condominium flat of similar size can sell quite differently.
ZIP codes: 90094

### Westchester (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/westchester)
Westchester is a City of Los Angeles community on the mesa north of LAX, home to Loyola Marymount University and bordered by Playa del Rey, Playa Vista, Ladera Heights and Inglewood. Executors and families here usually need date-of-death values for tract homes held since the 1950s, Prop 19 transfer support, and values that properly account for aircraft noise.
Housing: Growth came with the aircraft industry and Loyola's move to the area in 1928, and in the late 1930s Fritz Burns and Fred W. Marlow began building inexpensive homes near Manchester Avenue and Sepulveda Boulevard. Named areas such as Kentwood, Westport Heights and Loyola Village are mostly single-family houses on standard city lots, many since enlarged or rebuilt. Homes along the northern bluffs can have views over Playa Vista and the Ballona Wetlands.
Appraisal considerations: Jet noise led the City to buy out and remove thousands of homes near LAX, including the Manchester Square tract, so a subject's position relative to the runways and flight paths needs paired-sales testing. Homes nearest the airport may have had sound insulation work, which should be noted, and comparables should come from a similar noise setting. Expanded homes and ADUs are common, so permitted area should be verified before adjustments are made.
ZIP codes: 90045

### Marina del Rey (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/marina-del-rey)
Marina del Rey is an unincorporated Los Angeles County community built around a small-craft harbor that was dedicated in 1965 and is surrounded by the City of Los Angeles, between Venice and Playa del Rey. Most valuation requests here involve condominiums: date-of-death values for units held in trusts, divorce valuations of harbor-view homes, and family sales where the remaining ground-lease term must be understood.
Housing: Los Angeles County owns the land around the harbor and leases parcels to developers, so the condominium and apartment buildings along Via Marina and Admiralty Way sit on long-term ground leases rather than fee-owned land. The housing within the county area is almost entirely apartment and condominium buildings, including high-rise towers, many with harbor views. The adjoining Marina Peninsula and the Golden Triangle between Admiralty Way, Washington Boulevard and Lincoln Boulevard share the 90292 ZIP code and the Marina del Rey name, but they lie in the City of Los Angeles, where homes do not sit on county ground leases.
Appraisal considerations: Because the County owns the land, condominiums inside the county area are leasehold interests, and the remaining lease term, any extension and the lease's transfer provisions belong in the analysis alongside association dues and reserves. Comparables should match the subject's ownership type, since fee-simple sales from the City of Los Angeles side of the 90292 ZIP code can differ meaningfully from leasehold sales. Low-lying parcels near the water and Ballona Creek should also be checked for flood-zone status as of the effective date.
ZIP codes: 90292

### Baldwin Hills (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/baldwin-hills)
Baldwin Hills is a City of Los Angeles neighborhood on and below the Baldwin Hills between Culver City and Leimert Park, bounded roughly by La Cienega Boulevard, Crenshaw Boulevard and Stocker Street. Heirs, trustees and attorneys here ask for date-of-death values on hillside homes in Baldwin Hills Estates, trust valuations of Village Green condominiums, and buyout values for Baldwin Vista houses held by several family members.
Housing: Baldwin Hills Estates, locally called the Dons because nearly every street name begins with Don, climbs the slopes with hillside houses, many with swimming pools. Baldwin Vista, on the north side of the hills between La Cienega and La Brea, has houses developed in the 1950s. Village Green, completed in 1942 as Baldwin Hills Village and designed by Reginald D. Johnson with Clarence Stein, is a garden-city complex that now operates as a condominium association, while Baldwin Village holds mid-century apartment complexes. Modern condominiums built into steep hillsides add another product type.
Appraisal considerations: The neighborhood adjoins the Inglewood Oil Field, and the 1963 failure of the Baldwin Hills Dam was later linked to ground subsidence from oil and water extraction, so slope stability, drainage and distance to active wells deserve attention on hillside lots. Village Green is a National Historic Landmark whose owners association must approve nearly any modification to a unit, which makes resales within the complex the primary comparables. Homes backing onto open brush, where a 1985 fire destroyed dozens of houses in Baldwin Hills Estates, should be checked for fire-zone status and insurance terms.
ZIP codes: 90008, 90016

### Leimert Park (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/leimert-park)
Leimert Park is a City of Los Angeles neighborhood east of Crenshaw Boulevard, laid out from 1928 by developer Walter H. Leimert under a master plan by the Olmsted Brothers. Families and trustees here typically need date-of-death values for long-held period houses, Prop 19 analysis for a parent-to-child transfer, and buyout values when siblings inherit a home together.
Housing: The residential streets are known for Spanish Colonial Revival houses from the neighborhood's early decades, set along tree-lined blocks. Leimert Park Village, the commercial core around Leimert Plaza Park, Degnan Boulevard and 43rd Street, anchors the original plan. Published boundaries differ, with some maps extending the neighborhood north to Exposition Boulevard and east to Arlington Avenue, so a subject's exact location matters when comparables are chosen. Because so many houses date from the same era, differences in remodeling, original detail and lot position usually matter more than age.
Appraisal considerations: Individual Historic-Cultural Monuments exist here, including a single-family house on Olmstead Avenue, so designation status should be confirmed for any older house before redevelopment is assumed. For effective dates before the K Line opened in October 2022, comparables should reflect conditions along Crenshaw Boulevard at that time rather than today's transit access. Interior photos matter a great deal in a desktop review here, since original tile, woodwork and plaster detail can separate a restored house from one remodeled without regard to its period.
ZIP codes: 90008

### West Adams (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/west-adams)
West Adams is a historic district of the City of Los Angeles centered on Adams Boulevard and generally described as running from Pico Boulevard south to Jefferson Boulevard; most of its buildings went up between 1880 and 1925, when it ranked among the city's wealthiest areas. Heirs and attorneys here regularly need date-of-death values for period houses inside preservation zones, retrospective values for homes held in one family for decades, and buyout values for duplexes and large older houses shared by relatives.
Housing: Victorian mansions and Craftsman bungalows are the most familiar house types, joined by Queen Anne, Shingle, Colonial Revival, Mission Revival and Spanish Colonial Revival designs. Harvard Heights, built mainly between 1902 and 1910, is known for two-story Craftsman houses, and Jefferson Park holds roughly 2,500 homes built from 1905 to 1920, many of them bungalows. Lafayette Square, opened in 1913 around St. Charles Place, and West Adams Heights, laid out in 1902 with wide, contoured streets, hold some of the district's largest houses. Construction of the Santa Monica Freeway in the early 1960s cut through West Adams Heights, the area long called Sugar Hill, and removed many homes.
Appraisal considerations: Several Historic Preservation Overlay Zones cover parts of the district, including Harvard Heights and Lafayette Square (both adopted in 2000), West Adams Terrace (2003), Adams-Normandie (2010) and Jefferson Park (2011), so exterior changes require review and comparables should ideally come from within the same overlay. Properties with a Mills Act contract receive a property-tax reduction in exchange for preservation commitments, so the contract's terms should be identified and considered. Homes near the Santa Monica Freeway should be tested against interior-street sales for any noise or access effect.
ZIP codes: 90018, 90016, 90019

### View Park–Windsor Hills (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/view-park-windsor-hills)
View Park–Windsor Hills is an unincorporated Los Angeles County community of about 1.8 square miles, bordered by the City of Los Angeles, Culver City and Inglewood, with the Windsor Hills neighborhood lying north of Slauson Avenue. Families, trustees and attorneys here most often need date-of-death values for long-held family homes, Prop 19 analysis for transfers to children, and divorce valuations of remodeled hillside houses.
Housing: The Los Angeles Investment Company, also the developer of Hancock Park, built out View Park between 1923 and 1970, so its streets mix Spanish Colonial Revival and Mediterranean Revival houses with mid-century designs. Windsor Hills was developed beginning in the late 1930s by the Marlow-Burns Development Company, with Spanish Colonial Revival, Mediterranean Revival and minimal traditional houses. Architects whose work appears here include Paul R. Williams, Raphael Soriano, Robert Earl and Homer C. Valentine. The housing is predominantly single-family, much of it on sloping hillside lots.
Appraisal considerations: The View Park Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2016, covers homes built from the 1920s to the 1960s roughly bounded by Mount Vernon, Enoro, Northland and Northridge drives and Kenway, Victoria and Floresta avenues, so a subject's position inside or outside it should be noted. As an unincorporated community, permits, ADUs and lot splits are handled by Los Angeles County rather than a city, which matters when verifying added living area. Homes nearest Kenneth Hahn State Recreation Area and the adjoining Inglewood Oil Field should be tested for any proximity effect with local sales.
ZIP codes: 90043

### Ladera Heights (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/ladera-heights)
Ladera Heights is an unincorporated Los Angeles County community, with a small section inside the City of Los Angeles, set between Culver City, Baldwin Hills, View Park–Windsor Hills, Westchester and Inglewood. Requests here commonly involve date-of-death values for custom homes held since the 1960s, trust administration for houses on the hillside streets, and buyout values when heirs share a property.
Housing: Development began in the late 1940s in the small area east of La Cienega Boulevard and south of Slauson Avenue known as Old Ladera, and custom homes followed in the 1960s in what became known as New Ladera. Builders Valentine and Gallant were prominent, and designer Robert Earl drew many of the Valentine homes, including houses along Wooster Avenue on the community's western edge. Upper Ladera lies north of Slauson between La Cienega and Shenandoah Avenue, while the larger Lower Ladera spreads south of Slauson between Wooster and La Cienega.
Appraisal considerations: Because most of Ladera Heights is unincorporated, building permits, ADUs and lot splits fall under Los Angeles County, while the small City of Los Angeles section follows city rules, so the subject's jurisdiction should be confirmed before added living area is credited. The community sits beside the Inglewood Oil Field, which Los Angeles County regulates through the Baldwin Hills Community Standards District, so distance to wells and pump sites may be a location factor worth testing. Custom homes vary widely in size and design, so adjustments for quality and floor plan should rest on comparable custom-built sales rather than tract homes.
ZIP codes: 90056

### City of Los Angeles (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/los-angeles)
The City of Los Angeles covers roughly 469 square miles, reaching from the San Fernando Valley across the Santa Monica Mountains to the Westside, Downtown, South Los Angeles, and the harbor at San Pedro. Because one municipality holds so many separate housing markets, the questions heirs, trustees, and family-law attorneys bring us depend on the address: a date-of-death value for a Valley ranch house, a past-date value for a hillside home, or a buyout figure for a Downtown condominium.
Housing: The housing stock spans Victorian and Craftsman houses in the oldest neighborhoods, 1920s Period Revival districts, postwar ranch tracts across the San Fernando Valley, and modern homes on the slopes of the Santa Monica Mountains and Hollywood Hills. Condominiums and townhomes concentrate Downtown, in Koreatown, along Wilshire Boulevard, and on the Valley's major boulevards, and Playa Vista adds a newer planned district near the coast. Lots range from compact urban parcels and narrow hillside sites to estate properties in Bel Air and Brentwood, and the city had designated 35 Historic Preservation Overlay Zones as of 2023.
Appraisal considerations: For any address in the city, we check Historic Preservation Overlay Zone status, Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone mapping on hillside parcels, and permit history for accessory dwelling units and garage conversions. In Pacific Palisades, effective dates before and after the January 2025 Palisades Fire call for different evidence, from pre-fire sales of improved homes to later lot sales. Duplexes and other multi-unit properties fall outside desktop scope, so the legal use is confirmed first.
ZIP codes: 90002, 90003, 90004, 90005, 90006, 90007, 90008, 90010, 90011, 90012, 90013, 90014, 90015, 90016, 90017, 90018, 90019, 90020, 90021, 90023, 90024, 90025, 90026, 90027, 90028, 90029, 90031, 90032, 90033, 90034, 90035, 90036, 90037, 90038, 90039, 90041, 90042, 90043, 90044, 90045, 90046, 90047, 90048, 90049, 90057, 90062, 90064, 90065, 90066, 90067, 90068, 90071, 90077, 90094, 90272, 90291, 90293, 90710, 90731, 90732, 90744, 91040, 91042, 91303, 91304, 91306, 91307, 91311, 91316, 91324, 91325, 91326, 91331, 91335, 91342, 91343, 91344, 91345, 91352, 91356, 91364, 91367, 91401, 91402, 91403, 91405, 91406, 91411, 91423, 91436, 91601, 91602, 91604, 91605, 91606, 91607

### Downtown Los Angeles (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/downtown-los-angeles)
Downtown Los Angeles is the city's civic and financial center, a dense grid of districts running from Bunker Hill and the Historic Core to South Park, Little Tokyo, and the Arts District beside the Los Angeles River. Almost every owner-occupied home here is a condominium or loft, so executors, trustees, and divorcing owners usually ask us to value a single unit as of a past date, often with questions about the building's association finances.
Housing: Bunker Hill was lowered and rebuilt in the late twentieth century with modern high-rises, and South Park has since added a cluster of residential towers and hotel-branded condominiums at L.A. Live, some held as condominiums and others as rental apartments. In the Historic Core and the Arts District, office, department-store, and industrial buildings from the early 1900s became lofts after the city adopted its Adaptive Reuse Ordinance in 1999, which produced more than 14,000 units within a decade. Detached houses are essentially absent; the nearest single-family streets lie in surrounding neighborhoods such as Angelino Heights and Boyle Heights.
Appraisal considerations: Converted loft buildings differ in how units are held, some as recorded condominiums and others as rentals, so the condominium map, CC&Rs, and HOA documents are reviewed before comparables are chosen. Sales in the same building near the effective date get first priority, with adjustments for floor, view, parking spaces, and dues. Buildings with special assessments, litigation, or deferred repairs are kept separate from comparables without those issues.
ZIP codes: 90012, 90013, 90014, 90015, 90017, 90021, 90071

### Hollywood (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/hollywood)
Hollywood incorporated in 1903 and consolidated with Los Angeles in 1910, and today it runs roughly from Franklin Avenue and Hollywood Boulevard south to Melrose Avenue, between Western Avenue and La Brea Avenue or the West Hollywood line. Beyond its entertainment landmarks, it holds small tracts of 1910s and 1920s houses and a large condominium stock, so families and attorneys bring us historic-district bungalows, inherited condos, and past-date values for trust funding.
Housing: Single-family streets cluster in a few historic tracts: Spaulding Square, built between 1916 and 1921 with mostly Colonial-style bungalows; Sunset Square, with Craftsman, Spanish Colonial Revival, and American Colonial Revival houses; and Hollywood Grove, a foothill enclave of Craftsman and Colonial Revival bungalows. Above Franklin Avenue, Whitley Heights was designed between 1918 and 1928 as a Mediterranean-style hillside village. Elsewhere, apartment buildings from many decades fill most blocks, joined by newer low- and mid-rise projects, and condominiums are a common form of ownership housing.
Appraisal considerations: Hollywood's Historic Preservation Overlay Zones include Whitley Heights, Spaulding Square, Hollywood Grove, and Sunset Square, where exterior changes require review, and Whitley Heights is also listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The Hollywood Freeway split Whitley Heights when it was built, and homes close to the 101 are measured against sales in similar freeway-adjacent locations. Condominiums are matched within the same building or with buildings of similar age and amenities.
ZIP codes: 90028, 90038, 90046, 90068

### Hollywood Hills (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/hollywood-hills)
