The Hollywood Hills rise above Hollywood in the eastern Santa Monica Mountains, straddling the Cahuenga Pass and the 101 Freeway from Laurel Canyon east to Griffith Park, with Mulholland Drive along the ridge. Heirs and trustees here usually need values for individual hillside houses, where views, access, and lot conditions vary so much that comparable selection becomes the central question.
Housing: Development came in waves. Subdivisions of the 1920s such as Hollywoodland in upper Beachwood Canyon, Outpost Estates, and Whitley Heights favored Spanish, Mediterranean, and storybook designs on hillside lots, and later decades added modernist houses, some on very steep sites. Laurel Canyon grew from an early-1900s vacation colony into a neighborhood of houses from many eras, and Mount Olympus, developed in the 1960s, has wider streets and larger homes. The area has one of the lowest population densities in the city, and its upper streets are lined almost entirely with detached houses on irregular lots.
Appraisal considerations: Each hillside parcel is reviewed for Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone status, street access, slope, and buildable area, because two similar-looking houses can differ sharply on those points. The January 2025 Sunset Fire near Runyon Canyon was contained within about a day and evacuation orders were lifted the next morning; for effective dates that week, we confirm the property was unaffected and review how pending sales closed. Decks, additions, and converted spaces on older homes are checked against permit records.
ZIP codes: 90068, 90046, 90069

### Los Feliz (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/los-feliz)
Los Feliz stretches from Griffith Park south to Hollywood Boulevard and Fountain Avenue, and from Western Avenue east to the Los Angeles River, with Los Feliz Boulevard separating the hillside estates to the north from the shops and apartment blocks around Los Feliz Village. Trustees and heirs here often hold long-owned hillside houses or architect-designed homes, and attorneys ask us for past-date values that account for each property's setting and architecture.
Housing: North of Los Feliz Boulevard, the Los Feliz Hills and Los Feliz Estates hold larger hillside houses, and the Los Feliz Heights tract, subdivided in 1921, is known for American Colonial, Spanish Colonial, Mediterranean, and Tudor Revival homes built between 1920 and 1949. Laughlin Park is a gated enclave of about 60 houses. Modernist landmarks include Frank Lloyd Wright's Ennis House and Richard Neutra's Lovell Health House. To the southeast, Franklin Hills climbs into steep streets linked by public staircases, while apartment buildings and some condominiums fill many blocks south of the boulevard.
Appraisal considerations: Hillside parcels next to Griffith Park are reviewed for fire-hazard zoning, access, and slope; a 2007 wildfire burned about 800 acres of open terrain in Los Feliz and the park. For designated landmarks or homes by noted architects, we look beyond the immediate neighborhood for sales of comparable significance and explain the reasoning. Sales inside gated Laughlin Park are compared first with each other.
ZIP codes: 90027

### Silver Lake (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/silver-lake)
Silver Lake is a hilly neighborhood east of Hollywood, bounded roughly by the Hollywood Freeway, Virgil Avenue, the Glendale Freeway, and the Los Angeles River, and it is centered on the Silver Lake and Ivanhoe reservoirs. Families and attorneys bring us hillside houses with views, modernist homes by recognized architects, and small-lot homes that need careful comparable selection.
Housing: Ivanhoe, north of the reservoir, was laid out in 1887 with many streets named after figures from British literature, and Moreno Highlands around the water was developed in the 1920s and 1930s. Modernist architects including Richard Neutra, Rudolph Schindler, John Lautner, Gregory Ain, and Raphael Soriano designed homes and studios here. Public staircases climb many of the steeper streets, and newer small-lot homes and some lofts sit among older bungalows and apartment buildings.
Appraisal considerations: View premiums vary widely; a direct reservoir view, a partial view, and a downslope house below street level each call for different comparables. Small-lot homes are owned fee-simple but typically share access driveways and maintenance agreements, so they are compared with other small-lot sales rather than with conventional houses. On the steepest streets, limited parking and long climbs from the curb can narrow the buyer pool, so we look for sales with the same constraints.
ZIP codes: 90026, 90039

### Echo Park (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/echo-park)
Echo Park lies just northwest of Downtown Los Angeles, a hilly neighborhood whose few level areas include the basin around Echo Park Lake, with Elysian Park and Dodger Stadium along its eastern edge. Heirs, trustees, and attorneys here bring us hillside houses, Victorian homes in a historic district, and newer small-lot homes, often for date-of-death or buyout values.
Housing: Angelino Heights, founded in 1886, holds the city's densest concentration of 19th-century Victorian houses, centered on Carroll Avenue, along with Craftsman and Mission Revival homes. Elysian Heights, between the lake and Elysian Park, is known for steep streets and stairways, and its designated monuments include the Atwater Bungalows. Elsewhere, bungalows and cottages stand among small apartment buildings, newer small-lot subdivisions, and the gated hillside community of Hathaway Estates.
Appraisal considerations: Angelino Heights became the city's first Historic Preservation Overlay Zone in 1983, so exterior changes there are reviewed and comparables come first from inside the district. On hillside lots, we check access, slope, buildable area, and permit history for additions and decks. Small-lot homes are valued against other small-lot sales.
ZIP codes: 90026

### Hancock Park (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/hancock-park)
Hancock Park is a residential district between Melrose Avenue and Wilshire Boulevard, from Highland Avenue east to Rossmore Avenue, surrounding the grounds of the Wilshire Country Club. It sits within a cluster of historic neighborhoods that includes Windsor Square and Larchmont Village, and estate attorneys, trustees, and families bring us long-held homes that call for careful past-date valuation.
Housing: Residential development under the Hancock Park name began around 1919 on land G. Allan Hancock inherited from the former Rancho La Brea, and most homes are two-story 1920s residences in Tudor, English, Spanish Colonial, Mediterranean, Monterey, and American Colonial Revival styles. Deep front setbacks of about 50 feet are typical, and many lots route the driveway along one side, under a porte cochere, to a garage at the rear. Windsor Square, developed from 1911, adds Tudor, Italian Renaissance, and Dutch Colonial Revival homes and the mayor's official residence, Getty House. To the southwest, Brookside holds about 400 homes, mostly in Period Revival styles, on eight streets developed beginning in 1920.
Appraisal considerations: The Hancock Park HPOZ, adopted in 2008, and the Windsor Square HPOZ, adopted in 2004, review exterior changes, and historic-district status also bears on whether SB 9 lot splits are available. Owners in an HPOZ may be eligible for Mills Act tax contracts, so we ask whether one is recorded. Large-lot and country-club comparables are rare, so we document every adjustment.
ZIP codes: 90004, 90005, 90020

### Miracle Mile (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/miracle-mile)
Miracle Mile centers on the stretch of Wilshire Boulevard that developer A. W. Ross shaped in the 1920s into a car-oriented commercial district, now known for its Museum Row. The residential blocks north and south of Wilshire hold period houses, duplexes, and apartment buildings, and families and fiduciaries ask us to value single-family homes and condominiums there as of past dates.
Housing: The Miracle Mile HPOZ, covering about 1,347 properties between Wilshire and San Vicente boulevards and La Brea and Orange Grove avenues, has mostly one-story single-family homes north of Olympic Boulevard and one- and two-story multifamily buildings south of it. Its styles include Spanish Colonial, Tudor, Mediterranean, French, and American Colonial Revival, plus Minimal Traditional houses and Mid-Century apartments. North of Third Street, the Miracle Mile North HPOZ holds uniform one-story homes built from 1924 to 1941, more than half of them Spanish Colonial Revival. Park La Brea, a large rental apartment community, was built by Metropolitan Life beginning in the 1940s.
Appraisal considerations: Both HPOZs require review of exterior changes, which shapes additions and second-story plans. South of Olympic, many lots hold duplexes and other multi-unit buildings, so we confirm a property is a single-family home or condominium before accepting it for a desktop report. For effective dates before the subway stations opened, we use sales from the construction years rather than assuming the finished line's effect.
ZIP codes: 90036, 90019

### Koreatown (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/koreatown)
Koreatown sits about three miles west of Downtown, officially bounded by Vermont Avenue, Western Avenue, Third Street, and Olympic Boulevard, on generally flat land along Wilshire Boulevard. Most of the housing here is rental, so the ownership market is concentrated in condominiums, and the requests we receive from heirs and attorneys typically involve one condo unit, or one of the area's few houses, for an estate or a divorce.
Housing: The stock is overwhelmingly multifamily. Older apartment buildings line many blocks, historic Art Deco buildings with terra cotta facades survive along the commercial streets, and a wave of construction since the early 2000s added mid-rise and high-rise apartment and condominium buildings, with high-rises concentrated along Wilshire Boulevard between Western and Vermont. Ownership units are mostly condominiums, in buildings that range from older low-rise complexes to modern towers. Detached houses are scarce within the official boundaries; the nearest substantial single-family stock lies just west in Wilshire Park, where one- and two-story houses and some duplexes went up mostly between 1908 and 1926.
Appraisal considerations: For condominiums, we review HOA dues, reserves, special assessments, and any litigation, and give first weight to sales in the same building. Houses in nearby Wilshire Park, an HPOZ since 2008, are compared first with other homes in that district. Many older parcels hold duplexes or apartment buildings, which a desktop report does not cover, so the property type is verified from public records at the outset.
ZIP codes: 90005, 90006, 90010

### Mount Washington (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/mount-washington)
Mount Washington is a hillside neighborhood of Northeast Los Angeles, bordered by Eagle Rock, Highland Park, Cypress Park, and Glassell Park. It began in 1909 as Robert Marsh's subdivision around the Mount Washington Hotel, then reached by a funicular railway, and families here often need date-of-death or trust values for individual hillside houses where slope and access shape the analysis.
Housing: Homes sit on irregular hillside lots along winding streets, and they span many building eras, from houses built in the years after the 1909 subdivision to recent construction. On the steepest streets, houses often sit well above or below the roadway, with decks, terraced yards, and limited parking. Eldred Street, on the northeast side, is counted among the steepest streets in Los Angeles. The 2000 census found Mount Washington the least densely populated neighborhood in Northeast Los Angeles, consistent with its hillside lots and winding streets.
Appraisal considerations: Slope, street condition, usable lot area, and fire-hazard zoning are reviewed parcel by parcel, and decks, additions, and lower-level rooms are checked against permit records. Downslope and upslope houses are compared with similar configurations where possible. Vacant land is outside desktop scope, and a house with extensive unpermitted construction is better served by an inspection-based appraisal.
ZIP codes: 90065, 90042

### Highland Park (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/highland-park)
Highland Park is a Northeast Los Angeles neighborhood along the Arroyo Seco, laid out in 1886 and annexed to Los Angeles in 1895, with York Boulevard and Figueroa Street as its main corridors. Its large inventory of historic houses brings heirs, trustees, and attorneys to us for date-of-death and buyout values that take historic-district rules and restoration quality into account.
Housing: The Highland Park-Garvanza HPOZ is the city's largest, with about 4,000 structures in styles popular from the 1880s through the 1940s: Queen Anne, Shingle, Craftsman, Mission Revival, and Tudor Revival. The Arts and Crafts movement left many Craftsman bungalows, and Garvanza, annexed in 1899, has its own early-twentieth-century homes. Lots range from flat blocks near Figueroa to hillside parcels toward Mount Washington and Montecito Heights, and small apartment buildings mix with single-family streets.
Appraisal considerations: Exterior changes inside the HPOZ require review under the 2010 preservation plan, which affects additions, window replacements, and new construction. Because a property in the zone can carry a Mills Act contract, the title documents are checked for one. Hillside parcels toward Mount Washington are compared with other sloping lots rather than flat-land bungalows, and a duplex or other income property would need a different kind of assignment.
ZIP codes: 90042

### Eagle Rock (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/eagle-rock)
Eagle Rock fills a valley in Northeast Los Angeles between Glendale and Pasadena, edged on the west and north by the Glendale and Ventura freeways and named for the great boulder at the north end of Figueroa Street. It incorporated as its own city in 1911 and joined Los Angeles in 1923, and heirs, trustees, and attorneys bring us long-held family houses and hillside homes that need values as of a date of death or separation.
Housing: A Los Angeles Railway trolley line up Eagle Rock Boulevard and along Colorado Boulevard set off the valley's suburban growth, and the neighborhood keeps many historic homes in Craftsman, Georgian, Mission Revival, Art Deco, and Streamline Moderne styles, along with 19 designated Historic-Cultural Monuments. Bungalows and period houses line the flatter blocks near the boulevards, while streets on the surrounding hillsides add homes with views across the valley. Occidental College, which moved to its Myron Hunt-designed campus here in 1914, occupies a large site within the neighborhood.
Appraisal considerations: Eagle Rock has no Historic Preservation Overlay Zone, but individually designated monuments carry their own review requirements, so we confirm any designation. On the slopes toward the San Rafael Hills, we note each parcel's grade, driveway access, and fire hazard designation, and for homes beside the 134 or 2 freeways, the comparables share that exposure. Permit records are reviewed for garage conversions and accessory dwelling units.
ZIP codes: 90041

### Atwater Village (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/atwater-village)
Atwater Village is a compact Northeast Los Angeles neighborhood on the Los Angeles River flood plain, bounded by the Ventura Freeway on the north, the railroad tracks on the east, and the river on the south and west, with Griffith Park across the water. Its long-held houses bring estate attorneys, trustees, and families to us for date-of-death, trust, and buyout values.
Housing: The land was subdivided and sold to home builders in 1902, and the neighborhood became a sought-after residential area during the 1920s, with early residents including workers at a nearby power substation. Because few of its buildings have been torn down, Atwater Village has one of the largest counts of pre-1939 structures in Los Angeles County, and its level streets are lined largely with houses from those early decades. Glendale Boulevard serves as the commercial street, and the north end borders North Atwater Park and the La Kretz Bridge, a pedestrian crossing to Griffith Park completed in 2020.
Appraisal considerations: Because the neighborhood sits on the river's flood plain, we review current flood zone mapping for each parcel. Many houses are close to a century old, so the age and updating of foundations, systems, and finishes, documented in client photos, carry real weight in the analysis. Accessory units and garage conversions are checked against permit records, and houses on the blocks beside the Ventura Freeway are measured against sales with similar traffic exposure.
ZIP codes: 90039

### Boyle Heights (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/boyle-heights)
Boyle Heights rises on the bluffs east of the Los Angeles River, directly across from Downtown, and is named for Andrew Boyle, who built a home overlooking the river in 1858. Heirs, trustees, and attorneys come to us for date-of-death values and sibling buyouts on long-held houses, often with questions about how freeways and transit affect a particular block.
Housing: Settlement on the bluffs began in the mid-1800s and the neighborhood filled in over the following decades, so many homes sit on compact, older city lots. Detached houses share blocks with duplexes, small apartment buildings, and several large housing complexes, and some streets climb the hills and bluffs above the river, where lots slope. Adaptive reuse appears as well: the former Linda Vista Community Hospital is now the Hollenbeck Terrace Apartments.
Appraisal considerations: Several freeways converge at the East Los Angeles Interchange in Boyle Heights, so homes near the freeways are compared with similarly affected sales rather than with quiet interior blocks. Because some lots hold a second house or rear unit, we confirm the legal use from public records before accepting an order: a desktop report covers a single-family home, including one with a permitted accessory unit, but not a duplex or larger income property. For older houses, client photos of the interior and systems are especially important.
ZIP codes: 90033, 90023, 90063

### El Sereno (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/el-sereno)
El Sereno occupies the eastern corner of the City of Los Angeles, about four square miles bordering South Pasadena, Alhambra, and Monterey Park, with Huntington Drive and Valley Boulevard as its main corridors. Families and fiduciaries bring us long-held family houses, hillside homes, and properties along the former State Route 710 corridor, often for date-of-death or trust values.
Housing: Subdivisions followed the Pasadena Short Line, which opened in 1902; the area joined Los Angeles in pieces in 1912 and 1915, and 1920s tracts were built in Period Revival styles, while early schools and civic buildings used Mission and Craftsman designs. Wartime and postwar construction expanded the housing stock, especially at the southern end. The El Sereno-Berkshire HPOZ, adopted in 2017, protects an early tract of Craftsman, bungalow, Colonial Revival, and Spanish Colonial Revival homes near the South Pasadena border, and University Hills, named by the city in 2004, surrounds the Cal State LA campus.
Appraisal considerations: Caltrans acquired homes in El Sereno for a northern I-710 extension that was later abandoned, and houses sold by the state can carry recorded conditions on resale or occupancy. We review the deed and any recorded covenants before relying on such a sale as a comparable or valuing a home bought from the state. Homes on the hills above Huntington Drive are matched with hillside sales instead of valley-floor tracts, and the Berkshire HPOZ affects exterior changes inside its boundaries.
ZIP codes: 90032

### East Los Angeles (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/east-los-angeles)
East Los Angeles is an unincorporated community of about 7.5 square miles governed by Los Angeles County, bordered by Boyle Heights and El Sereno to the west and north, Monterey Park to the northeast, and Commerce and Montebello to the south and east. Most homes we value here have been in one family for decades, and the work is usually for an estate, a trust, or a buyout among heirs.
Housing: Belvedere Heights was subdivided in 1905, and Belvedere Gardens was laid out in 1921, with development accelerating in the early 1920s as workers in nearby industries sought housing. City Terrace, in the northern part, sits on the Repetto Hills, with steep, winding streets lined by Spanish Colonial Revival houses. Elsewhere, single-family houses, some with rear units or additions, share the street grid with small apartment buildings.
Appraisal considerations: County zoning and permitting apply, so we review Los Angeles County records rather than City of Los Angeles records for permits, accessory dwelling units, and unpermitted additions. Some lots hold a second dwelling, so the legal use is verified in county records before an order is accepted. For houses next to the 60 or 710, we look for comparables with the same freeway exposure.
ZIP codes: 90022, 90063

### Burbank (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/burbank)
Burbank sits at the eastern end of the San Fernando Valley, between the Verdugo Mountains and Griffith Park, and has been an incorporated city since 1911. Home to Warner Bros., the Walt Disney Studios, and Hollywood Burbank Airport, it combines single-family neighborhoods with apartment and condominium buildings, and trustees, heirs, and divorcing couples come to us for estate, trust, and settlement valuations on homes from the flatlands to the foothills.
Housing: Burbank divides into a flatland section and a downtown and foothill section rising toward the Verdugo Mountains. Magnolia Park on the west side was subdivided in the early 1920s, but most of its houses date to the 1940s, when tracts were built for returning veterans, as wartime employment at Lockheed's Burbank plant gave way to a postwar building boom. The Rancho Equestrian District near Griffith Park allows horses on residential lots and mixes single-family homes with some condominiums and townhomes. Condominiums and townhomes in other parts of the city add an attached segment to the ownership market.
Appraisal considerations: Magnolia Park lies beneath the airport's flight path, so we compare homes there with sales that share similar exposure. In the Rancho, horse-keeping zoning, stables, and lot size make in-district sales the primary evidence, while foothill homes below the Verdugo Mountains, where view, grade, and fire hazard zoning come into play, are grouped with other foothill sales. Before any added living area is counted, we confirm converted garages and accessory units through city permit records.
ZIP codes: 91501, 91502, 91504, 91505, 91506

### Glendale (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/glendale)
Glendale lies between Burbank and Pasadena, reaching from its downtown and the flatlands of south Glendale north through the Verdugo Mountains and San Rafael Hills into the Crescenta Valley. Incorporated in 1906, it is one of the county's larger cities, and probate attorneys, trustees, and families ask us to value everything from hillside houses to downtown condominiums for date-of-death, gift, and divorce purposes.
Housing: In south Glendale, which includes the former town of Tropico, many single-family homes were replaced by apartment and condominium buildings in the 1980s, and downtown high-rises and the Americana at Brand, opened in 2008, added more apartments and condominiums. Hillside neighborhoods such as Adams Hill in south Glendale and Chevy Chase Canyon in the San Rafael Hills hold single-family homes on sloping lots, and the city's historic districts protect concentrations of early houses, such as the Tudor Revival cottages of Cottage Grove at the foot of Adams Hill. Northern Glendale extends into the Crescenta Valley, taking in Verdugo City, Crescenta Highlands, and part of Montrose.
Appraisal considerations: Glendale has designated five historic districts, Rossmoyne, Brockmont Park, Royal Boulevard, Cottage Grove, and Ard Eevin Highlands, where design guidelines govern exterior changes, and individual properties may be listed on the Glendale Register of Historic Resources. Condominiums are compared with sales in the same or similar buildings after a review of HOA finances. Homes high in the Verdugo Mountains or San Rafael Hills raise fire-zone, grade, and access questions that flat-land sales cannot answer, so their comparables come from similar terrain.
ZIP codes: 91201, 91202, 91203, 91204, 91205, 91206, 91207, 91208, 91214

### La Cañada Flintridge (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/la-canada-flintridge)
La Cañada Flintridge is a foothill city in the Crescenta Valley at the western edge of the San Gabriel Valley, incorporated in 1976 when the communities of La Cañada and Flintridge combined, with NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory at its eastern end. Most requests we receive here involve houses a family has owned for decades, valued for a trust or an estate, including effective dates around the January 2025 Eaton Fire evacuations.
Housing: Flintridge, named for its developer, Senator Frank P. Flint, occupies the northern slopes of the San Rafael Hills, generally south of Foothill Boulevard, where winding streets follow the terrain. North of Foothill, residential streets climb toward the San Gabriel Mountains, where the Angeles Crest Highway begins its ascent. Development was slow for decades because water was scarce, and today the city's housing is overwhelmingly owner-occupied, much of it on streets shaded by native California live oaks.
Appraisal considerations: The city as a whole is classified as a Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone because of its terrain and oak cover, and nearly the entire city was evacuated during the January 2025 Eaton Fire, which destroyed many homes in neighboring Altadena. For effective dates in early 2025, we confirm whether the home had smoke or other damage and give weight to sales that closed after the fire. Parcels below canyon mouths are also reviewed for flood and debris-flow exposure.
ZIP codes: 91011

### La Crescenta–Montrose (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/la-crescenta-montrose)
La Crescenta–Montrose is an unincorporated area of about 3.4 square miles in the Crescenta Valley, bordered by Glendale to the south and west, La Cañada Flintridge to the east, and the Angeles National Forest to the north. Because its streets interlace with Glendale's and share the same mailing names, heirs and trustees often need help confirming jurisdiction before we value a long-held family home as of a date of death.
Housing: The name traces to early settler Benjamin Briggs, who saw three crescent-shaped formations from his home, and Montrose began as a subdivision named by contest in 1913. Suburban building started with that subdivision and accelerated after World War II, leaving residential streets of detached houses that rise toward the mountains, with much of the valley floor above 1,500 feet. Apartments and condominiums also form part of the housing mix. The Foothill Freeway crosses the southern part of the area, and Foothill Boulevard runs east to west through the valley.
Appraisal considerations: Addresses with La Crescenta or Montrose mailing names may lie in Glendale or in unincorporated county territory, so we confirm jurisdiction from assessor and county records before reviewing zoning and permits. On upper streets near the Angeles National Forest, we review the state's fire hazard maps, and near canyon outlets or flood-control channels we look at flood and debris-flow exposure, a concern dating to the destructive 1934 New Year's flood. Houses backing onto the Foothill Freeway are matched with sales that share that exposure.
ZIP codes: 91214, 91020

### Studio City (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/studio-city)
Studio City fills the southeast corner of the San Fernando Valley between the Los Angeles River and the Santa Monica Mountains, and it is named for the studio Mack Sennett opened here in 1927. Executors and family-law attorneys often need past-date values on hillside homes with long remodel histories or on flatland houses that were later rebuilt.
Housing: The flatlands on both sides of Ventura Boulevard mix Spanish, Traditional and ranch houses from the 1920s through the 1950s with a growing share of full rebuilds, mostly on level lots shaded by mature trees; Colfax Meadows and the Silver Triangle are two familiar flatland pockets. South of the boulevard, Fryman Estates and Wrightwood Estates climb into terraced lots with multilevel plans and Valley views. Condominium buildings, many dating from the 1970s and 1980s, appear north of the boulevard, including along Moorpark Street, and several Rudolph Schindler designs survive in the community.
Appraisal considerations: Hillside comparables must match slope, access, view and permitted square footage, because neighboring lots can differ sharply in utility. Parcels near Mulholland Drive may fall under the Mulholland Scenic Parkway Specific Plan, and a 2018 independent analysis tied FAA NextGen changes to more Hollywood Burbank Airport departures over areas south of the 101.
ZIP codes: 91604, 91602

### Sherman Oaks (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/sherman-oaks)
Sherman Oaks covers the Valley floor south of Van Nuys and the north slope of the Santa Monica Mountains, where the Los Angeles Suburban Homes Company subdivided about 1,000 acres in 1927. Trustees, conservators and divorcing spouses frequently need values tied to a specific earlier date, sometimes one close to the 1994 earthquake.
Housing: North of Ventura Boulevard, flatland tracts such as Chandler Estates and Magnolia Woods, a 45-block area moved from Van Nuys into Sherman Oaks in 1991, hold mid-century ranch homes and earlier bungalows, many enlarged or replaced. South of the boulevard, the terraced streets of the Sherman Oaks Hills hold custom homes, some with sweeping Valley views. Condominium buildings from the 1970s and 1980s line Dickens Street, a block north of Ventura.
Appraisal considerations: The 1994 earthquake struck Sherman Oaks hard, and nine stilt-supported hillside houses slid downslope, so past-date assignments may need to reflect a home's repair status on the valuation date. Condominium comparables should come from buildings of similar age and amenities, and lots backing onto the 405 or 101 warrant a test for freeway-noise influence.
ZIP codes: 91403, 91423, 91401

### Encino (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/encino)
Encino rises from the Sepulveda Basin up the north slope of the Santa Monica Mountains and takes its name from Rancho Los Encinos, established here in 1845. Trustees and estate attorneys often need date-of-death and step-up values on large-lot homes, and families weighing Prop 19 transfers or sibling buyouts ask for figures they can defend.
Housing: Encino's flatter streets mix postwar ranch and mid-century houses with condominium and townhome complexes, and new construction has replaced original houses in several areas, particularly south of the boulevard. Amestoy Estates and Royal Oaks are known for unusually large lots, some approaching an acre, with gated traditional, modern and farmhouse-style estates, pools and, on the biggest sites, tennis courts. South of Ventura Boulevard, Encino Hills and the roads toward Mulholland Drive add hillside sites with Valley views.
Appraisal considerations: On large lots much of the value lies in the land, so comparables should bracket usable site area as well as house size, and SB 9 split or ADU potential should be evaluated parcel by parcel rather than assumed. Gated estates may have few true peers in a given year, which can justify reaching into Sherman Oaks or Tarzana with documented location adjustments.
ZIP codes: 91316, 91436

### Tarzana (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/tarzana)
Tarzana stretches from Victory Boulevard south to Topanga State Park, on land Edgar Rice Burroughs bought in 1919 and later subdivided for homes and small farms. Its mix of modest flatland houses, golf-course estates and guard-gated hillside communities means heirs and trustees often need help choosing comparables that truly fit the property.
Housing: North of Ventura Boulevard, the flats hold smaller ranch and mid-century houses, many built from the 1940s through the 1960s, along with duplexes, condominium buildings and gated townhome complexes. South of the boulevard, lots grow toward half an acre and beyond, with Spanish Revival, Tudor, ranch and mid-century modern homes on the lower hillside streets. Melody Acres, a private enclave of ranch-style homes, is known for generous parcels. Higher up, the gated communities of Mulholland Park, Braemar Country Club Estates and Monte Verde Estates contain larger custom homes with canyon and Valley views.
Appraisal considerations: Gated hillside homes should be compared first within the same gate, since association services, private road upkeep and view corridors differ from one enclave to the next. Parcels near Topanga State Park should be checked against current fire hazard severity mapping, and lots facing Ventura Boulevard or the 101 can show traffic influence.
ZIP codes: 91356

### Woodland Hills (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/woodland-hills)
Woodland Hills occupies the southwest corner of the San Fernando Valley, from Warner Center's office towers to the edge of the Santa Monica Mountains and the Calabasas line. Founded as Girard in 1922 and renamed in 1945, it brings estate, trust and dissolution assignments that range from Warner Center condominiums to hillside homes with long Valley views.
Housing: Developer Victor Girard laid out the original town and planted roughly 120,000 trees, and century-old trees still shade some of the older streets. North of the boulevard, postwar tracts include Corbin Palms, a mid-1950s Palmer & Krisel design built by the George Alexander Construction Co., while Walnut Acres, on former orchard land, offers noticeably larger lots. South of Ventura, hillside streets hold custom, mid-century and newer contemporary homes, and condominium and apartment growth concentrates in and around Warner Center under the 2035 plan the city adopted in 2013.
Appraisal considerations: Corbin Palms homes are best compared with other intact mid-century houses where possible, since original design features and sensitive remodels matter to that buyer pool. Hillside sales south of Ventura should share the subject's grade, outlook and driveway access, and the large Walnut Acres lots are worth reviewing for ADU or SB 9 potential without assuming either is feasible.
ZIP codes: 91364, 91367

### West Hills (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/west-hills)
West Hills took its name in 1987, when residents of western Canoga Park petitioned the city for a separate identity, and it runs from the Chatsworth Reservoir south toward Woodland Hills against the Simi Hills and the Ventura County line. Executors and trustees here typically ask for date-of-death and step-up values on 1960s tract homes and on newer gated houses at the community's north end.
Housing: Much of West Hills stayed agricultural long after the rest of the Valley urbanized; Platt Ranch was not tied into the Los Angeles water system until 1958 and saw little building before 1961. The resulting stock leans toward 1960s mid-century tracts on lots up to roughly a quarter acre, including Woodlake Estates and Pinelake Estates on the former Peppergate Ranch, followed by 1980s and 1990s Spanish-style houses, some within homeowner associations. Townhome and condominium complexes from the 1970s and 1980s add an attached option, and a manufactured-home community sits in the foothills near the Canoga Park line.
Appraisal considerations: The 2018 Woolsey Fire began on the Santa Susana Field Laboratory property near the Ventura County line and forced evacuations in West Hills, so wildland-edge parcels deserve a check of current fire hazard severity mapping. Homes backing to open space along the western and northern edges often trade differently from interior tract houses and should be compared with sales in a similar setting.
ZIP codes: 91307, 91304

### Canoga Park (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/canoga-park)
Canoga Park began in 1912 as the townsite of Owensmouth, joined Los Angeles in 1917 and took its present name in 1931. Estate and trust work here often centers on postwar ranch houses held by one family for decades, while divorce and buyout assignments frequently involve condominiums and townhomes near Warner Center.
Housing: Most single-family homes date from the post–World War II building boom, typically one-story ranch houses on standard lots, many since enlarged or rebuilt. The Main Street Canoga Park district along Sherman Way marks the original Owensmouth townsite, and a share of the community's houses predate World War II. Condominium and townhome complexes add an attached option along several boulevards, and the community's southern edge shares in Warner Center's newer apartment construction.
Appraisal considerations: Garage conversions, unpermitted additions and newer ADUs are common in older tracts, so we compare permitted square footage from public records with what the photos show and treat unpermitted space conservatively. Parcels next to industrial corridors, the G Line busway or heavily traveled boulevards should be compared with similarly situated sales rather than interior-block homes.
ZIP codes: 91303, 91304

### Reseda (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/reseda)
Reseda sits in the middle of the west San Fernando Valley, bounded roughly by Roscoe Boulevard, White Oak Avenue, Victory Boulevard and Corbin Avenue, and it was founded in 1912 as Marian before taking its present name in the early 1920s. Families settling an estate or dividing property here usually need values on modest single-story houses, often with additions, garage conversions or back units that must be sorted out first.
Housing: Farming kept much of Reseda in lettuce, lima beans, sugar beets and walnuts until World War II, when the large ranches were subdivided and single-family construction surged through the late 1940s and 1950s. The result is a largely flat grid of one-story ranch houses, bungalows and mid-century homes on modest lots. Earlier houses from the 1920s and 1930s remain in two areas, the blocks southwest of the Reseda Boulevard and Sherman Way intersection and the Reseda Ranch tract by Grover Cleveland High School, while most newer construction has taken the form of condominiums and townhomes along the major boulevards.
Appraisal considerations: The 1994 Northridge earthquake's epicenter lay just west of Reseda Boulevard between Arminta and Ingomar streets, and the 1971 San Fernando quake also shook the community, so older houses may carry repair, foundation or retrofit history worth documenting. Garage conversions and back units are common; we separate permitted from unpermitted space and test any ADU contribution against actual sales rather than assumed rents.
ZIP codes: 91335

### Northridge (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/northridge)
Northridge spreads across the north-central San Fernando Valley around California State University, Northridge, on land settlers called Zelzah in 1908 before the Northridge name took hold in the late 1930s. Executors, trustees and attorneys here often need date-of-death or retrospective values on long-held postwar houses, and some assignments still turn on how a property fared in the 1994 earthquake that carries the community's name.
Housing: After World War II, agricultural acreage was subdivided into suburban tracts for returning veterans, and one-story ranch and mid-century houses remain the core of the housing stock. Sherwood Forest is known for larger lots shaded by mature evergreens, and Palmer & Krisel designed a 1959 modern tract here as well. Newer construction includes the Mosaic community of contemporary homes in south Northridge, while condominiums, townhomes and apartments, the last common near the CSUN campus, round out the stock.
Appraisal considerations: The 1994 earthquake collapsed the Northridge Meadows apartments and heavily damaged the Fashion Center and CSUN, and many surrounding homes were repaired or rebuilt afterward, so past-date work should note structural history where records show it. Where a larger parcel is zoned for horse keeping, comparables should share that use rather than come from standard tract lots.
ZIP codes: 91324, 91325

### Porter Ranch (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/porter-ranch)
Porter Ranch occupies the hilly northwest tip of the San Fernando Valley, rising from Northridge toward the Santa Susana Mountains along Porter Ranch Drive, Tampa Avenue and Rinaldi Street. Heirs, trustees and family-law attorneys here often need values on newer, association-governed homes, and some questions reach back to the 2015–2016 Aliso Canyon gas leak or the 2019 Saddleridge Fire.
Housing: Building began with tract homes in the early 1960s, and later phases climbed into the foothills with ranch, split-level and Spanish-influenced houses on generous lots. The gated Renaissance community, built by Shapell Homes and opened in 1999 at the neighborhood's highest point, holds large homes in Spanish Colonial, Italianate and Tuscan styles. More recently, Toll Brothers' Porter Ranch master plan has added villages such as Westcliffe, Hillcrest and Bella Vista with large single-family homes, while condominiums and townhomes give buyers an attached option.
Appraisal considerations: The Aliso Canyon storage-field leak discovered in October 2015 led SoCalGas to temporarily relocate thousands of households before the well was plugged in February 2016, and the field remains in operation at reduced capacity, so retrospective values near those dates call for sales from the same period. The 2019 Saddleridge Fire burned homes in the eastern part of the community, making Fire Hazard Severity Zone status, insurability and HOA obligations relevant to many hillside comparisons.
ZIP codes: 91326

### Granada Hills (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/granada-hills)
Granada Hills spreads across the north San Fernando Valley from the Santa Susana foothills down past the 118 freeway, on land that was once the Sunshine Ranch dairy and orchards. Founded as Granada in 1926, it brings estate, trust and Prop 19 assignments centered on long-held mid-century houses, some in a historic overlay where design rules matter.
Housing: Most homes were built in the 1950s and 1960s, and one-story postwar ranch houses dominate, with pockets of two-story tracts and architect-designed modern houses; remnant citrus trees still stand in many yards. Balboa Highlands, an Eichler tract built from 1962 to 1964 to designs by A. Quincy Jones, Frederick Emmons and Claude Oakland, became a Historic Preservation Overlay Zone in 2010. Foothill streets near Bee Canyon and O'Melveny Park offer more varied lots and views, the Knollwood Country Club area forms another recognized pocket, and townhome communities such as Woodley Village add an attached choice.
Appraisal considerations: Exterior changes in Balboa Highlands generally go through HPOZ review, so unapproved alterations or a sensitive restoration can affect marketability, and those homes should be compared with other Eichlers rather than generic tracts. The 1971 quake forced a four-day evacuation of about 80,000 people below the damaged Lower Van Norman Dam, and the 1994 quake shook Granada Hills severely, so older files may note foundation or chimney repairs worth confirming.
ZIP codes: 91344

### Chatsworth (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/chatsworth)
Chatsworth occupies the northwest corner of the San Fernando Valley, where the Simi Hills and Santa Susana Mountains close in around rocky outcrops and the old Chatsworth Reservoir. Its name traces to an 1888 subdivision, and today executors and trustees bring a mix of tract-house, gated-estate and horse-property valuations.
Housing: Most homes are suburban: mid-century houses on grid streets near the older business district, ranch houses through the central tracts, and newer two-story homes on cul-de-sacs. Lots grow larger toward the outer edges, where stables and corrals appear on parcels zoned for equine keeping. Gated Indian Springs Estates and Hidden Oaks hold estate-sized homes, Deer Lake Highlands offers hillside sites, and Deerlake Ranch, a 230-acre master plan just north of the 118, adds roughly 300 single-family homes in phases completed from about 2020 onward, with townhomes such as Rockpointe providing attached options.
Appraisal considerations: Lots zoned RA, RE20, RE40, A1 or A2, or within a K district, fall under city equine-keeping rules that limit how close new living space can be built to stables, so additions and ADUs need case-by-case review. Foothill parcels bordering open space may carry a Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone designation that bears on insurance and brush clearance, and the newer Deerlake Ranch homes belong with recent tract sales rather than older custom properties.
ZIP codes: 91311

### Van Nuys (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/van-nuys)
Van Nuys, founded in 1911 and annexed to Los Angeles in 1915, serves as the San Fernando Valley's civic center, anchored by the 1932 Valley Municipal Building and surrounded by blocks of older single-family homes. Trustees, executors and family-law attorneys bring assignments ranging from 1940s bungalows to condominiums, frequently with garage conversions or rear units that have to be sorted out first.
Housing: Single-family building began with the 1911 townsite, and the Van Nuys Historic Preservation Overlay Zone, adopted in 2005 as the Valley's first HPOZ, protects Craftsman, Colonial Revival, Spanish Colonial Revival and English Revival houses alongside later Minimal Traditional and ranch designs. Much of the remaining single-family stock consists of 1940s and 1950s bungalows, cottages and ranch houses on modest lots, many expanded over the years. Apartments account for a large share of the housing, and condominium and townhome complexes give buyers an attached choice.
Appraisal considerations: Van Nuys Airport, with two parallel runways, ranks among the busiest general aviation airports in the world, so homes beneath arrival and departure paths should be compared with sales in a similar noise setting. Inside the HPOZ, exterior alterations require review, and garage conversions and rear units elsewhere should be checked against permit records before any value is assigned to them.
ZIP codes: 91405, 91406, 91411, 91401

### North Hollywood (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/north-hollywood)
North Hollywood grew from a townsite laid out in 1887, later called Lankershim, and adopted its current name in 1927; today it surrounds the NoHo Arts District and the North Hollywood station, northern terminus of the Metro B Line. Heirs and trustees often hold postwar bungalows owned by one family for decades, while family-law matters frequently involve newer condominiums and townhomes near the transit hub.
Housing: Postwar bungalows and Minimal Traditional houses with detached garages still fill many tree-lined side streets, and some older homes date to the early 20th century, when the area was known for its peach orchards. Apartment buildings typically line the main boulevards with houses on the streets behind them, and new condominiums and townhomes arrive mostly as in-fill on existing parcels. A few developers have also built larger Modern Traditional homes.
Appraisal considerations: Zero-lot-line homes, newer townhomes and older condominium buildings create a wide range of attached product, so comparables should match ownership type, age and parking. On single-family lots, rear units and garage conversions are common and should be checked against permit records, and homes near the airport approach or rail and freeway corridors should be compared with similarly affected sales.
ZIP codes: 91601, 91605, 91606

### Valley Village (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/valley-village)
Valley Village lies between Burbank Boulevard, the Tujunga Wash, the Ventura Freeway and the Hollywood Freeway, an area long counted as part of North Hollywood until homeowners organized for a separate identity in the mid-1980s; the city marked its borders with blue signs in 1991. Families and trustees here typically need values on single-story houses held for decades, while divorce and buyout assignments often involve the neighborhood's many condominiums.
Housing: Workers at nearby film studios built houses here in the 1930s, and the single-family stock remains mostly one-story Spanish and ranch-style homes on tree-lined interior streets. Apartment and condominium buildings concentrate along the main boulevards; a 1985 campaign against oversized "stucco mountains" led the city to recommend a three-story limit, and development is now also guided by the Valley Village Specific Plan. Some older houses have given way to infill condominium projects, among them a home Marilyn Monroe occupied in the mid-1940s, demolished in 2015.
Appraisal considerations: Because Valley Village mixes single-family streets with apartments and condominiums, comparables should match the immediate setting, and homes backing to multifamily buildings, the 101 or the 170 often need a location adjustment. ZIP codes overlap with North Hollywood, Studio City and Sherman Oaks, so we confirm neighborhood boundaries before relying on listing labels.
ZIP codes: 91607, 91601

### Toluca Lake (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/toluca-lake)
Toluca Lake is a compact community at the southeast edge of the Valley, bordered by Universal City, Studio City, North Hollywood and Burbank, and it spills across the city line into Burbank around a small, privately owned lake. Executors and trustees here often hold long-owned period homes or lake- and golf-adjacent estates for which few direct comparables trade in any given year.
Housing: Investors launched Toluca Lake Park in 1923, and the Toluca Lake Company later promoted the area as a bedroom community; surviving homes from those decades include Spanish Colonial and Colonial-style houses. Homes ring the lake beside the Lakeside Golf Club, which Max Behr designed in 1924, and Case Study House No. 1, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, stands in the community. Apartment and condominium buildings make up a substantial attached segment.
Appraisal considerations: Lakefront and golf-course lots rarely change hands, and the lake is private and maintained by a property owners association, so those sites need a longer look-back and careful paired comparisons with nearby interior lots. Burbank-side homes fall under a different city's permits and schools, and Hollywood Burbank Airport traffic can influence some blocks, so both factors should be tested before sales are mixed.
ZIP codes: 91602

### Sylmar (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/sylmar)
Sylmar is the northernmost neighborhood in the City of Los Angeles, rising from San Fernando Road toward the San Gabriel foothills between the 5 and 210 freeways, on land whose olive orchards were described in 1906 as the largest olive grove in the world. Heirs and trustees here bring a wide range of properties, from tract homes on cul-de-sacs to half-acre parcels with stables, along with occasional questions about the 1971 earthquake or the 2008 Sayre Fire.
Housing: The ground climbs from about 1,100 feet near San Fernando Road to roughly 1,700 feet at Hubbard Street, and the north side has steep residential streets with Valley views. Mid-century ranch houses make up much of the stock, followed by contemporary Spanish-style homes from the 1990s and early 2000s, many on curving streets ending in cul-de-sacs; the hilly northwest section is known as Rancho Cascades. Sylmar is also one of the few parts of the city where single-family homes on half-acre lots remain, many with corrals for horses, while gated condominium and townhome communities, along with manufactured housing, round out the mix.
Appraisal considerations: The 2008 Sayre Fire destroyed most of the Oakridge Mobile Home Park, and homes along the foothill edge warrant a look at state fire-hazard mapping, insurance availability and brush-clearance obligations. Where a parcel keeps horses, the city's equine-keeping standards set minimum separations between stables and new habitable space, which can constrain an ADU, an addition or an SB 9 split.
ZIP codes: 91342

### Sunland-Tujunga (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/sunland-tujunga)
Sunland-Tujunga occupies the western end of the Crescenta Valley between the Verdugo Mountains and the San Gabriel Mountains, with Mount Gleason Avenue marking the traditional line between Sunland to the west and Tujunga to the east. Sunland joined Los Angeles in 1926 and Tujunga followed in 1932, and estate and trust assignments here often involve older owner-built homes, sloping lots and parcels near the wildland edge.
Housing: Tujunga traces its roots to the Little Landers, an early-20th-century utopian colony organized around small farm plots. Owner-builders arrived in numbers after the First World War, and many set their houses on foundations of boulders collected nearby. Boulder and river-rock construction survives on some of those older houses, which share the area with homes from the postwar decades. Hillside and canyon streets, including the small Riverwood enclave, hold homes on sloping lots with mountain views, while Foothill Boulevard, the main commercial corridor, is governed by its own specific plan.
Appraisal considerations: The 2009 Station Fire burned in the mountains near Sunland-Tujunga, and the 2017 La Tuna Fire reached into the area from the Verdugo Mountains, so Fire Hazard Severity Zone status and brush-clearance duties matter for many hillside comparisons. Owner-built additions and older stone construction often lack complete permit records, which calls for careful reconciliation of recorded area, and parcels with horse-keeping rights call for a check of the stable-to-dwelling separations the city enforces.
ZIP codes: 91040, 91042

### San Fernando (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/san-fernando)
San Fernando is a compact incorporated city of about two and a third square miles, completely surrounded by the City of Los Angeles, with Sylmar to the north, Lake View Terrace to the east, Pacoima to the south and Mission Hills to the west. Incorporated in 1911, it takes its name from Mission San Fernando Rey de España, and families settling estates or arranging Prop 19 transfers here usually own modest older houses, sometimes with a second unit on the lot.
Housing: The housing stock runs from 1920s Craftsman bungalows through postwar ranch houses to two-story stucco homes added in the early 2000s, with the occasional larger Mediterranean-style house. Most parcels are modest in size, though a few run considerably larger. Gated townhome communities and condominiums add attached options, while accessory dwelling units and second dwellings appear on some single-family parcels.
Appraisal considerations: The 1971 San Fernando earthquake struck the city at extreme intensity and severed buried utility lines throughout it, so older homes may carry foundation repair or retrofit history worth confirming in the records. Because ADUs and second dwellings are common, we confirm permitted status and recorded unit counts before treating a rear unit as income-producing or contributory living area, and comparables may be drawn from adjoining Los Angeles neighborhoods when the city's own sales are thin.
ZIP codes: 91340

### Santa Clarita (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/santa-clarita)
Santa Clarita incorporated in 1987 by joining Canyon Country, Newhall, Saugus, and Valencia, and it has since grown through annexations across the Santa Clarita Valley. Estate and family work here spans original-owner tract homes, condominiums and townhomes in large associations, canyon parcels with horse keeping, and buyouts when one heir stays in a home bought new decades earlier.
Housing: Newhall holds the valley's oldest blocks around its historic downtown, while Saugus and Canyon Country filled with single-family tracts from the 1960s onward. Valencia's master-planned villages added townhomes, condominiums, and detached homes linked by paseos. Sand Canyon keeps larger rural and equestrian parcels, manufactured-home communities add another ownership type, and newer subdivisions such as Skyline Ranch and Vista Canyon extend the city's edges.
Appraisal considerations: Many newer tracts carry Mello-Roos or other special-tax assessments and association dues, which we document because buyers weigh total carrying cost. Canyon and foothill parcels near the Angeles National Forest face wildfire exposure; the 2016 Sand Fire alone burned nearly 42,000 acres around Canyon Country. Manufactured homes and equestrian parcels need comparables that match their ownership and use.
ZIP codes: 91321, 91350, 91351, 91354, 91355, 91387, 91390

### Valencia (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/valencia)
Valencia is the master-planned core of the City of Santa Clarita, laid out from the 1960s by the Newhall Land and Farming Company, with McBean Parkway as its main north–south road and the Valencia Town Center at its center. Executors here often need values for homes bought new from the original builder, townhomes in large associations, and properties whose special taxes affect what buyers will pay.
Housing: The first subdivision, the original Old Orchard tract near Lyons Avenue, opened in 1967, followed by Valencia Hills and a long series of villages built over the next decades. Villages cluster around schools and parks and are linked by paseos that cross major streets on bridges and underpasses. Detached tract homes, townhomes, and condominiums sit side by side, many under their own associations.
Appraisal considerations: Valencia east of Interstate 5 is largely within the City of Santa Clarita, while areas west of the freeway that carry the Valencia name, including FivePoint Valencia, are unincorporated, so we confirm jurisdiction and taxing districts. Many villages layer a master association over a sub-association plus Mello-Roos or other special taxes, and we document each charge.
ZIP codes: 91354, 91355

### Stevenson Ranch (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/stevenson-ranch)
West of Interstate 5 in the foothills of the Santa Susana Mountains, Stevenson Ranch is an unincorporated community governed by Los Angeles County rather than the City of Santa Clarita. Families and trustees here usually bring us homes bought new in the late 1980s through the 2000s, properties carrying special taxes and association dues, and buyouts where one heir keeps the house.
Housing: Dale Poe Development began the community after the County approved its first phase in 1985, and construction ran through the late 1980s and 1990s, with Lennar acquiring the Poe interest in 1996. The census-designated place has two subdivisions: Westridge in the north, developed as part of Valencia, and Stevenson Ranch proper in the center and south. Most homes are detached houses on graded hillside lots, alongside townhome, condominium, and apartment complexes.
Appraisal considerations: As an unincorporated community, Stevenson Ranch falls under County planning, and we confirm special-tax districts and association dues for each property. Homes backing onto brush-covered slopes face wildfire exposure and brush-clearance rules, and sloped lots call for attention to usable yard area and retaining walls.
ZIP codes: 91381

### Calabasas (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/calabasas)
Incorporated in 1991, Calabasas sits along the Ventura Freeway at the western edge of the San Fernando Valley, where the Santa Monica Mountains meet the Las Virgenes corridor. Trustees and estate attorneys here commonly need values for large homes in gated communities, condominiums and townhomes held in trust, and older canyon properties with unusual access.
Housing: Much of the city consists of planned communities built from the 1960s through the 2000s, including Calabasas Park, Mountain View Estates, Calabasas Hills, and gated enclaves such as The Oaks and Calabasas Park Estates. Park Moderne, also called the Bird Streets, and the Calabasas Highlands hold older, more individual homes on hillside lots. Townhomes and condominiums, many in association-run complexes, form a sizable attached segment.
Appraisal considerations: Hillside and canyon parcels sit in wildfire-prone terrain, and the 2018 Woolsey Fire reached the city, damaging Grape Arbor Park, so we weigh brush-clearance duties, insurance availability, and any fire history of the parcel. Gated communities often carry master and sub-association dues, and older canyon homes may involve access easements or nonconforming improvements that need careful records review.
ZIP codes: 91302, 91301

### Agoura Hills (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/agoura-hills)
Agoura Hills incorporated in 1982 along the Ventura Freeway between Calabasas and Westlake Village, below the ridgelines of the Santa Monica Mountains. Estates here often hold tract homes bought new in the 1960s through the 1980s, horse properties in Old Agoura, or attached units placed in a family trust.
Housing: Growth began in the late 1960s after the Ventura Freeway reached the area, and the first tracts, including Hillrise, Liberty Canyon, and Lake Lindero, were followed by large subdivisions in the 1980s. Old Agoura, south of the freeway, keeps a semi-rural character with larger lots, horse facilities, and custom homes. Townhomes and condominiums sit near the freeway, while hillside streets look toward Ladyface Mountain.
Appraisal considerations: The 2018 Woolsey Fire burned through parts of the community, and hillside and canyon properties remain in high fire hazard areas, so we review rebuild status, brush clearance, and insurance where they apply. Equestrian parcels need comparables with similar zoning, acreage, and facilities, and homes near the freeway are tested for noise and traffic influence with paired sales.
ZIP codes: 91301

### Westlake Village (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/westlake-village)
Westlake Village is the Los Angeles County share of a master-planned community that straddles the Ventura County line; it incorporated in 1981 after about two-thirds of the original development had been annexed to Thousand Oaks. Trustees and heirs here often need values for lakefront homes, condominiums and townhomes, and houses in association neighborhoods, sometimes with family property on both sides of the line.
Housing: The American-Hawaiian Steamship Company bought the 12,000-acre ranch in 1963 and commissioned a master plan for a city in the country; development began in 1966 and the lake was completed in 1969. Housing includes lakefront residences, single-family neighborhoods, townhomes, condominiums, view estates, and mobile homes. The city describes about twenty neighborhoods with active homeowners associations, among them the First Neighborhood, Lakeshore, and Three Springs communities.
Appraisal considerations: A Westlake Village mailing address can fall in either county, so we confirm the county and city of each property. For lakefront homes we verify lake rights, dock access, and association rules, and dues and special assessments are documented for every neighborhood. Hillside parcels near open space, where the 2018 Woolsey Fire also burned, warrant attention to fire exposure.
ZIP codes: 91361, 91362

### Lancaster (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/lancaster)
Lancaster grew around an 1876 Southern Pacific water stop in the Antelope Valley, was mapped into streets and lots in 1884, and incorporated as a city in 1977, forming a twin-city pair with Palmdale to the south. Executors, trustees and family members here usually need values on tract homes in the city's subdivisions, from modest older houses near downtown to newer two-story homes on the west and east sides.
Housing: Lancaster's oldest neighborhoods sit near The BLVD downtown, where small houses from roughly the late 1930s through the early 1950s line streets such as Gadsden and Genoa avenues, many altered by garage conversions. Growth tied to Edwards Air Force Base spread mid-century ranch tracts outward in the 1950s and 1960s, and later waves added single-story and two-story stucco homes with tile roofs and multi-car garages, especially in West Lancaster, where lot sizes tend to run larger. Townhomes, condominiums and senior communities supply most attached housing, and since 2014 the city has required solar panels on new homes.
Appraisal considerations: Solar systems are common under the city's new-home requirement, so whether panels are owned, financed or leased should be confirmed, since leased equipment is not part of the real estate and owned systems are valued based on market evidence. Older downtown houses often show garage conversions or other alterations that need permit review, and larger west-side lots should be compared with sales offering similar site area.
ZIP codes: 93534, 93535, 93536

### Palmdale (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/palmdale)
Palmdale lies at the south end of the Antelope Valley, where the San Gabriel Mountains meet the high desert, and it grew from the 1886 Palmenthal settlement into a city that incorporated in 1962. Heirs and trustees here most often need values on tract and master-planned homes built during the 1980s and 1990s boom and the subdivisions that followed.
Housing: Rapid growth in the 1980s and 1990s brought large tracts of single-family homes, much of it on the west side around Rancho Vista Boulevard, where three- and four-bedroom houses built from the 1970s through the 1990s predominate. Anaverde, a master-planned community in west Palmdale, added newer homes with association amenities mainly in the 2000s and early 2010s, while East Palmdale, east of Sierra Highway, extends toward more rural surroundings, with larger parcels at its outer edges. Townhomes and condominiums form a smaller segment, and stucco exteriors with tile roofs are common.
Appraisal considerations: Palmdale sits beside the San Andreas Fault, so parcels near the fault trace may lie within a mapped earthquake fault zone that warrants disclosure review, and homes near Plant 42 can experience aircraft noise. Master-planned communities such as Anaverde carry association dues that buyers weigh, so comparables should come from tracts with similar fees, age and amenities.
ZIP codes: 93550, 93551, 93552

### Pasadena (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/pasadena)
Pasadena runs from the hillside streets of Linda Vista, across the Arroyo Seco, to Hastings Ranch below the foothills, with Old Pasadena and the Civic Center at its core. Heirs and trustees commonly bring us long-held houses in landmark districts, effective dates on either side of the January 2025 Eaton Fire, and sibling buyouts of the family home.
Housing: Craftsman bungalows fill Bungalow Heaven and Garfield Heights, Greene and Greene–era houses cluster near the Arroyo, and Spanish, Tudor, and Colonial Revival homes sit on larger lots in the southwest and Oak Knoll. Hastings Ranch filled in with postwar ranch houses, and townhomes and condominiums near downtown and the Metro A Line form a substantial attached market.
Appraisal considerations: Pasadena has more than a dozen landmark districts, a Mills Act program dating to 2002, and an ordinance excluding landmark districts from SB 9 lot splits that the state Attorney General has disputed. The Eaton Fire destroyed more than a hundred homes in the city, mainly in Upper Hastings Ranch, Victory Rose, and Dundee Heights; for those parcels, pre-fire dates rely on pre-fire sales, while later dates turn on lot value and the city's rebuild ordinance.
ZIP codes: 91101, 91103, 91104, 91105, 91106, 91107

### South Pasadena (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/south-pasadena)
South Pasadena covers about three and a half square miles beside the Arroyo Seco, bordered by Pasadena, San Marino, Alhambra, and Los Angeles, with Mission Street and its Metro A Line station at its center. Attorneys and executors here often need retrospective values for houses owned since the 1960s or earlier, sibling trust distributions, and Prop 19 transfers.
Housing: The stock spans Victorian and Shingle-style houses, a deep layer of Craftsman bungalows, 1920s Spanish Colonial, Tudor, and Mediterranean revivals, and mid-century modern homes. Single-family homes and multifamily units are split roughly evenly, with most apartments and condominiums in small buildings. In the Monterey Hills, where the city's redevelopment agency auctioned graded lots in 1962 for what became Altos de Monterey, curving hillside streets hold later construction.
Appraisal considerations: The city has a preservation ordinance, designated historic districts, and an Inventory of Historic Resources, so an older house may face review of exterior changes or carry a Mills Act contract. The end of the 710 Freeway extension has returned former Caltrans-owned houses to the market, some resold by the city under state rules directing proceeds to affordable housing, and those sales need screening before use as comparables.
ZIP codes: 91030

### San Marino (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/san-marino)
Formed in 1913 from ranch land that included Henry E. Huntington's estate, San Marino is a small, almost entirely residential city just south of Pasadena. Typical assignments include date-of-death values that set stepped-up basis on homes held for decades, gift and Prop 19 values for family transfers, and land-weighted analysis when an original house sits on a large parcel.
Housing: Most houses date from 1920 to 1950, in Spanish Colonial Revival, Tudor, Colonial Revival, and other period styles, with later ranch homes and contemporary rebuilds mixed in. The city is zoned into residential area districts by minimum lot size, from parcels of a few thousand square feet to estate districts where lots exceed an acre. Condominiums and townhomes are scarce.
Appraisal considerations: San Marino's strict design review covers new houses and significant exterior changes, shaping what a buyer can build and how long approval takes. Because many long-held properties pair an original house with a large lot, we often reconcile improved sales with a land analysis drawn from lot and teardown sales, noting the area district and any historic status.
ZIP codes: 91108

### Altadena (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/altadena)
Altadena is an unincorporated Los Angeles County community at the foot of the San Gabriel Mountains, directly north of Pasadena. The Eaton Fire, which began January 7, 2025, destroyed thousands of homes here, so many questions now straddle that date, from pre-fire values for 2024 deaths to cleared lots held by estates and heirs divided over rebuilding.
Housing: Before the fire, housing ran from 1880s mansions on Mariposa Street's Millionaire's Row to Craftsman bungalows, E. P. Janes's mid-1920s English and Spanish style houses in Janes Village, and postwar ranch homes on the upper slopes. Whole blocks are now cleared lots beside surviving homes, rebuilds, and finished new houses. The Altadena side of the Historic Highlands neighborhood, spared by the fire, became Los Angeles County's first historic district, covering 77 parcels.
Appraisal considerations: For effective dates before January 7, 2025, we value the property as it stood, using pre-fire sales plus photos, permits, and listing records to document lost improvements. For later dates, burned parcels are analyzed through vacant-lot sales, debris-removal status, and rebuild permits, and surviving homes are compared with other survivors. Insurance proceeds and litigation or utility recoveries are separate assets outside the real estate value.
ZIP codes: 91001

### Sierra Madre (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/sierra-madre)
Sierra Madre is a foothill city of about three square miles between Pasadena and Arcadia, with Sierra Madre Boulevard as its main street. Executors and family members here usually ask about long-held houses passing through a trust, canyon cabins with unusual access, and whether the 2025 Eaton Fire should influence a value even where the house came through untouched.
Housing: Older cottages and Craftsman bungalows line the grid near downtown, while later ranch and custom homes climb toward the foothills. In Lower and Upper Sierra Madre Canyon, small cabins and bungalows sit along narrow, winding roads, often on irregular lots with little parking. Apartments, duplexes, and a few condominium buildings add attached housing, but detached houses dominate.
Appraisal considerations: The Eaton Fire destroyed a small number of structures along Sierra Madre's northern edge and burned the wilderness above it, so retrospective work separates pre-fire and post-fire market conditions. For later effective dates, we note burn-scar debris-flow exposure and insurance availability for canyon and hillside parcels, and canyon lots call for close reading of lot lines, access easements, and older unpermitted additions.
ZIP codes: 91024

### Arcadia (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/arcadia)
Arcadia occupies former Rancho Santa Anita land that Lucky Baldwin acquired in 1875, reaching from the foothills south past Santa Anita Park and Huntington Drive. The estates we see here often hold original postwar ranch homes on generous lots or newer custom houses, and families need a defensible value before deciding whether to sell, rent, or rebuild.
Housing: Many of the city's chicken ranches became home lots after World War II, leaving ranch-style houses on wide parcels across the north and central city. Santa Anita Oaks, the Highlands, and the Rancho Santa Anita areas hold larger custom homes, and large new houses have steadily replaced original ones. Condominiums and townhomes are concentrated near downtown and in the southern part of the city.
Appraisal considerations: The city recognizes five homeowners associations whose Architectural Review Boards hold design authority over new homes and exterior changes, on top of city design guidelines and floor-area limits. Where builders would bid for the lot beneath an original house, we test both the improved value and the land value, and sales of brand-new homes need careful quality and condition adjustments.
ZIP codes: 91006, 91007

### Monrovia (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/monrovia)
Incorporated in 1887, Monrovia grew from a townsite centered on Myrtle Avenue and now runs from the San Gabriel foothills south across the 210 Freeway, where its Metro A Line station sits. Families settling estates here often hold turn-of-the-century houses, postwar homes held since new, or foothill properties, and attorneys may need values for buyouts or dates of separation.
Housing: The blocks around Old Town retain Victorian, Craftsman, and period revival houses, many with detached garages. Postwar ranch homes fill much of the rest of the city, while larger custom and view homes sit along the northern foothill streets. South Monrovia adds smaller tract homes, apartments, and townhomes, and the Station Square district around the A Line station brings newer attached housing.
Appraisal considerations: Some older Monrovia houses may be locally designated or carry Mills Act contracts, so we confirm historic status through city and county records. Foothill parcels need attention to slope, defensible space, and fire-hazard mapping, and deep lots in the older core may support an ADU or lot split, though parcel-level constraints decide whether that potential is real.
ZIP codes: 91016

### Duarte (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/duarte)
Below the San Gabriel foothills between Monrovia and the San Gabriel River, Duarte became a city in 1957, and Huntington Drive, the old Route 66, runs through its middle. Assignments range from postwar homes with a single owner since the early years to foothill houses near Bradbury and condominiums or townhomes left to several siblings.
Housing: Former citrus land was subdivided after World War II into modest single-story tract homes, much of which still forms the city's core. Larger homes on the northern slopes border the estate city of Bradbury, while later townhome and condominium communities and some newer infill sit closer to Huntington Drive. Lot sizes and terrain change noticeably from the flats to the canyon edges.
Appraisal considerations: ZIP code 91008 is shared with Bradbury, so we confirm whether a property lies in Duarte, Bradbury, or unincorporated territory before choosing comparables. Hillside parcels near the canyon mouths raise fire-hazard and vegetation-management questions, and association dues and amenities are documented for townhomes and condominiums.
ZIP codes: 91010, 91008

### Temple City (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/temple-city)
Walter P. Temple subdivided 400 acres of former Rancho Santa Anita land into affordable home lots in 1923, and the town he started incorporated as Temple City in 1960. Estate work here often involves modest original houses on deep lots and newer two-story homes, and heirs frequently ask whether a parcel supports an added unit before deciding to sell.
Housing: The original 1923 townsite, bounded roughly by Garibaldi, Baldwin, Live Oak, and Encinita avenues, keeps some of the earliest cottages, while postwar ranch homes cover most other blocks. Many lots are long and narrow, and many original houses have been replaced by larger two-story homes. Multifamily zones along the commercial corridors hold apartments, townhomes, and small clusters of detached units.
Appraisal considerations: Temple City adopted its own SB 9 standards, including a courtyard requirement between units that state housing officials have questioned, so lot-split potential has to be confirmed parcel by parcel. Where an older house sits on a deep lot, we compare it with sales of similar original homes and test whether land or development potential is driving value, and existing back units are checked against permits.
ZIP codes: 91780

### San Gabriel (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/san-gabriel)
San Gabriel grew up around Mission San Gabriel Arcángel, founded in 1771, and incorporated in 1913; it lies between San Marino, Alhambra, Rosemead, and Temple City. Estate and trust work here ranges from long-held homes near the mission to larger north-side houses and newer townhomes, and families often ask how a second dwelling on the lot affects value.
Housing: Older bungalows and Spanish Revival homes surround the Mission District, while streets north toward San Marino and the San Gabriel Country Club hold larger lots and later custom houses. Postwar single-story homes fill much of the central city. Older houses in multifamily zones have steadily given way to townhomes and small-lot detached projects, which add a steady supply of newer homes.
Appraisal considerations: Many lots hold more than one dwelling, so we compare the units on the parcel with permit and Assessor records before giving value to a back house. A San Gabriel mailing address does not always mean city limits, since surrounding unincorporated areas share the same ZIP codes, and we confirm jurisdiction before selecting comparables.
ZIP codes: 91775, 91776

### Alhambra (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/alhambra)
Long promoted as a city of homes, Alhambra incorporated in 1903 and sits just east of the El Sereno district of Los Angeles, with Main Street as its commercial spine.
