Executors here often handle 1920s houses held for generations, a parent's condominium, or a family sale where siblings want a supportable price before one buys out the others.
Housing: The single-family stock leans toward Craftsman bungalows and Spanish Colonial Revival and Mediterranean homes from the early twentieth century, and named tracts include the Bean Tract, the Airport Tract, and the Midwick Tract on the grounds of a former country club. Smaller postwar houses fill in toward the south. Multifamily zones hold a large inventory of condominium and townhome buildings, many replacing older houses on single lots.
Appraisal considerations: Homes along the San Bernardino Freeway in the south and near the end of the Long Beach Freeway at Valley Boulevard can show freeway influence, which we test with paired sales. For condominiums, we review association dues, special assessments, and building age, and for older houses we confirm whether additions and garage conversions were permitted.
ZIP codes: 91801, 91803

### Monterey Park (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/monterey-park)
Monterey Park incorporated in 1916 and borders Alhambra, Rosemead, Montebello, and East Los Angeles, with East Los Angeles College inside its limits and Cal State LA just beyond. Its estates commonly include postwar homes bought in the 1950s and 1960s, hillside houses with city views, and condominiums in newer mixed-use buildings, each calling for a different set of comparables.
Housing: The city's first subdivision, Ramona Acres, dates to 1906, though much of its housing went up after World War II, as new tracts and annexations pushed the city outward. Hillside streets in the Monterey Highlands and around the Garvey and Monterey Hills hold homes on sloping lots, some with long views across the basin. Townhomes and condominiums, including those in Atlantic Times Square, give the city a substantial attached segment.
Appraisal considerations: Hillside parcels call for attention to slope, usable lot area, retaining walls, and views, which we weigh with sales on similar terrain. Homes near the three freeways may show traffic or noise influence, gauged by comparing corridor sales with interior-street sales. For condominiums in mixed-use buildings, association dues, commercial neighbors, and parking arrangements can shape value.
ZIP codes: 91754, 91755

### Rosemead (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/rosemead)
Named for Leonard J. Rose's nineteenth-century horse ranch, Rosemead became a city in 1959 and sits between San Gabriel, Temple City, El Monte, and Monterey Park. Heirs here often bring us postwar houses kept in one family across generations, lots holding more than one home, and townhomes divided among siblings.
Housing: Single-story homes from the postwar decades make up most of the detached stock, and many sit on long, deep lots. A good number of parcels carry a back house or later additions. Townhome and small-lot detached projects have replaced some older houses in multifamily zones, giving buyers newer attached options alongside the original stock.
Appraisal considerations: Because deep lots and back units are common, we check permits and Assessor records for every structure and confirm whether zoning supports the existing unit count. Where a buyer would likely replace an older house with townhomes or additional units, land value and development constraints carry real weight.
ZIP codes: 91770

### El Monte (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/el-monte)
Known as the end of the Santa Fe Trail, El Monte incorporated in 1912 and lies between the Rio Hondo and the San Gabriel River in the center of the San Gabriel Valley. Valuation needs here often involve modest homes held for decades, lots with multiple units, and family sales where one heir buys out the rest.
Housing: The housing stock ranges from 1930s homes built under a federal subsistence homestead program to single-family houses spread across former walnut groves and farmland. Many lots are deep and narrow, and many carry additional units or later additions. Condominiums, townhomes, and newer small-lot developments appear near the downtown and transit corridors.
Appraisal considerations: Tenant occupancy is common, so we note whether a property was rented on the effective date, since leases can affect marketability. Permit history matters on lots with back units or conversions, and homes near the freeways and the airport may warrant a test for external influence.
ZIP codes: 91731, 91732

### South El Monte (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/south-el-monte)
South El Monte, incorporated in 1958, covers under three square miles between El Monte and the Whittier Narrows open space. A typical file involves a small single-family home with one long-term owner, a lot with an added unit, or a house beside industrial uses whose external influence must be measured.
Housing: Much of the housing consists of modest single-story homes, some on lots that also hold a second dwelling or later additions. Residential pockets sit among large industrial and commercial districts, and the city's overall housing stock is small. Newer townhomes and small gated developments have been added on infill parcels.
Appraisal considerations: Homes next to industrial or heavy commercial uses may show external influence from truck traffic, noise, or odors, which we measure against sales on interior residential streets. We confirm permits for any back units and check FEMA flood mapping, since the city borders the Whittier Narrows flood-control basin.
ZIP codes: 91733

### Azusa (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/azusa)
Azusa sits at the mouth of San Gabriel Canyon on the valley's northeast edge, crossed by Interstate 210 and served by two Metro A Line stations. Estate files here range from long-held tract houses near downtown to newer homes in Rosedale and the gated Mountain Cove enclave, and heirs often ask how those newer neighborhoods should be compared.
Housing: Pre-war houses and apartment buildings line the older core around downtown and Foothill Boulevard, and postwar one-story ranch houses on ordinary suburban lots fill much of the valley floor. Rosedale, developed mostly in the 2010s on former Monrovia Nursery land, added two-story Spanish, Craftsman and bungalow-style houses plus townhomes and condominiums under a homeowners association. Mountain Cove, reached by a bridge just inside San Gabriel Canyon, holds larger two-story homes from the early 2000s behind a gate.
Appraisal considerations: Rosedale and Mountain Cove homes are measured against sales inside their own association settings before anything else, with dues and any special assessments confirmed from the tax bill. Canyon-edge parcels on the northern margin call for a check of fire hazard severity zone status as of the effective date, and near downtown, added rooms and converted garages should match permit records before counting as living area.
ZIP codes: 91702

### Glendora (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/glendora)
Climbing from the valley floor across Interstate 210 into the San Gabriel foothills, Glendora was founded in 1887 and still centers on Glendora Village. Because many homes have stayed in one family for decades, trustees and attorneys often ask for past-date values, sometimes alongside a Prop 19 transfer or a sibling buyout.
Housing: Victorian and Craftsman houses cluster around the Village, Finkbiner Park, Bennett Avenue and Vista Bonita, joined by Mission Revival and 1930s period revival homes. From the late 1940s single-story ranch tracts spread east, while north Glendora's foothill streets added larger 1950s and 1960s ranch homes on generous lots, many with mountain or city views. Gated Gordon Highlands, in the eastern foothills, holds custom estates on acre-plus lots, while condominiums and townhomes occupy pockets of the flatter ground.
Appraisal considerations: Much of the foothill backcountry falls in the Very High category on the fire hazard map the city adopted in 2025, and the January 2014 Colby Fire destroyed homes on the northern edge, so hazard status and post-fire buyer response matter for past dates. Designated local landmarks face review of exterior changes and may carry Mills Act contracts. Acreage estates rarely have close local matches, so the search often reaches other foothill estate areas.
ZIP codes: 91740, 91741

### San Dimas (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/san-dimas)
Once called Mud Springs and incorporated in 1960, San Dimas stretches from Bonelli Regional Park north to San Dimas Canyon, with a downtown of wooden sidewalks and Western storefronts. Estates here can include horse properties, hillside homes and association-run townhomes.
Housing: Most neighborhoods date from the 1950s through the 1980s, when ranch tracts filled the flats and builders moved onto the slopes. Via Verde, around its country club in the south, curves across rolling ground on Spanish-named streets, while the northern foothills hold larger custom homes. A 1987 specific-plan subdivision near Baseline Road and Cataract Avenue was planned with shared equestrian facilities, and planned developments such as Sycamore Canyon added attached homes.
Appraisal considerations: Horse-keeping parcels with barns, arenas or trail access belong with other equestrian sales rather than standard tract homes. Sloped parcels fall under the city's hillside development chapter, which can require planning review before grading or additions, and foothill sites should be located on current state fire hazard maps. The small unincorporated West San Dimas area, surrounded by the city near Walnut Creek Park, follows county zoning rather than city rules.
ZIP codes: 91773

### La Verne (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/la-verne)
La Verne began as the 1887 railroad town of Lordsburg at the foot of the San Gabriel Mountains, and its Old Town still centers on the University of La Verne and D Street. Executors here bring everything from Old Town bungalows to canyon horse properties and condominiums.
Housing: Craftsman and Victorian homes from before about 1940 give Old Town and the neighboring Lordsburg blocks their character, mixed with early apartment buildings and newer houses designed to match. Mid-century ranch tracts and some condominium complexes cover much of the remaining city, and north La Verne adds larger traditional and semi-custom homes on rising ground. Off Live Oak Canyon Road near the Claremont line, Live Oak and Webb canyons hold mostly custom homes on large lots, horse properties among them.
Appraisal considerations: Most of north La Verne, Live Oak Canyon included, lies in a Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone. Exterior work in Old Town is governed by the Old Town La Verne and Lordsburg specific plans, which supply design review in place of a citywide preservation ordinance, and any Mills Act contract should be confirmed. Mobilehome park units, usually personal property on rented spaces, fall outside this kind of appraisal.
ZIP codes: 91750

### Claremont (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/claremont)
Seven Claremont Colleges, the shops of the Village and block after block of mature street trees define Claremont, incorporated in 1907 at the county's eastern edge below the San Gabriel foothills. Valuation questions here often involve architecturally significant houses, where preservation rules can matter as much as square footage.
Housing: Craftsman, Victorian and Spanish Colonial Revival houses from about the 1890s to the 1940s fill the grid around the Village and Pomona College. University Circle and other Old Claremont streets carried revival and early ranch styles into the postwar years, and Chaparral is largely 1960s and 1970s ranch construction, much of it by Lewis Homes. Hillside Claraboya, from the early 1960s, and Padua Hills, whose post-and-beam houses include two by Richard Neutra, carry modernism into the foothills, while condominiums, townhomes and senior communities such as Pilgrim Place form a smaller share.
Appraisal considerations: Homes on the Claremont Register or inside a historic district need a Certificate of Appropriateness for significant exterior work, and demolishing any building 45 years or older triggers city review. Mills Act contracts lower taxes but bind future owners, so their terms should be confirmed. Foothill lots also face rural-residential design standards and fire hazard mapping.
ZIP codes: 91711

### Pomona (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/pomona)
One of eastern Los Angeles County's oldest cities, Pomona incorporated in 1888 and is home to the Fairplex, Cal Poly Pomona and a historic downtown. Heirs here often want to know how a historic designation, a nearby freeway or a hillside lot affects the value of a long-held family home.
Housing: Pomona's three residential historic districts, Lincoln Park, Wilton Heights and Hacienda Park, protect older neighborhoods, with Lincoln Park alone holding hundreds of Victorian, Craftsman and period revival homes from the 1890s through the 1940s. On the northwest side, Ganesha Hills mixes early bungalows, ranch homes and newer construction on rolling ground with mountain views. Postwar single-story tracts account for much of the remaining housing, and Phillips Ranch, begun in 1965 by Louis Lesser Enterprises in the southwest hills, combines detached homes and attached housing on slopes edged by the SR-71.
Appraisal considerations: Contributing homes in the historic districts generally need preservation review for exterior changes, so designation effects and non-original alterations are judged against sales in the same district. Phillips Ranch and Ganesha Hills sales should be grouped by slope, view and freeway exposure rather than blended with valley-floor tracts. For dates before September 2025, transit influence should reflect what buyers then expected rather than the station that later opened.
ZIP codes: 91766, 91767, 91768

### Covina (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/covina)
Covina grew from orange and lemon groves into a postwar suburb between Interstate 210 and Interstate 10, keeping early-1900s buildings along Citrus Avenue. Most estate files involve long-held ranch homes, and the first question is often whether the address is inside city limits.
Housing: Bungalows survive near downtown, but most of Covina was built between the 1940s and the 1980s as single-story ranch tracts, many since enlarged. Charter Oak, on the northeast side, mixes postwar ranch houses with 1980s condominiums and townhomes, and part of it lies outside the city. Recent infill includes three-story townhomes and a flats-and-townhouse project on a former citrus processing site, and a few manufactured-home communities round out the stock.
Appraisal considerations: A Covina mailing address does not confirm city jurisdiction, because ZIP codes 91722 through 91724 reach into unincorporated county land and the city notes that street numbers of 3000 or higher are generally outside its limits. That distinction changes the rules for ADUs and lot splits. Homes backing to the rail corridor or downtown commercial frontage need similarly situated comparables, and assessor square footage on older ranch houses should be reconciled with permits.
ZIP codes: 91722, 91723, 91724

### West Covina (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/west-covina)
West Covina incorporated in 1923, largely to keep a neighboring city's planned sewage farm off its walnut and orange groves, and became one of the fastest-growing suburbs of the 1950s. Requests here center on mid-century ranch homes, San Jose Hills view properties and townhomes, frequently valued as of a date years back.
Housing: Tract building began with the 1941 Sunkist Village subdivision and surged after the war, blanketing northern and central West Covina with modest ranch homes. South of Interstate 10, the South Hills pair hillside ranch houses with Spanish and Mediterranean estates built from the 1980s into the 2000s. Woodside, mostly built in the 1970s, mixes ranch, split-level and two-story plans on curving streets, with condominium and townhome complexes at either end.
Appraisal considerations: Hillside parcels in the South Hills and near Galster Wilderness Park should be screened against fire hazard severity zone maps, and steep lots often offer less usable yard than their size suggests. Sales on opposite sides of Interstate 10 belong in separate groups, and for 1990s and early-2000s dates, builder sales of South Hills estates should be distinguished from resales.
ZIP codes: 91790, 91791, 91792

### Baldwin Park (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/baldwin-park)
Known as Vineland until it took Lucky Baldwin's name, Baldwin Park incorporated in 1956 on level ground east of the San Gabriel River, with Interstate 10 crossing the city. A parent's long-held 1950s house is the usual subject, often with additions or a second unit that heirs want explained.
Housing: Single-story mid-century homes on modest flat lots dominate, most built during the 1950s boom, with a few older Craftsman-era houses remaining. Newer construction is mostly infill, including Spanish-style townhomes, small gated communities such as Park Shadow, and affordable housing on Ramona Boulevard. Manufactured homes, including a gated land-lease park, add another product type, and over the years some owners have added rooms or second units.
Appraisal considerations: Second units and converted garages must be checked against city permits, since unpermitted space usually earns limited contributory value rather than full living-area credit. Homes along the freeways and rail corridor need similarly exposed comparables. For past dates, the state ADU reforms that began in 2017 and SB 9, effective in 2022, mean development potential must be judged under the rules then in force.
ZIP codes: 91706

### La Puente (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/la-puente)
Compact and mostly residential, La Puente incorporated in 1956 on former Rancho La Puente land once known for walnut groves and a large walnut packing plant. Because many La Puente addresses actually lie in unincorporated Valinda, West Puente Valley or Bassett, jurisdiction is confirmed before any date-of-death analysis begins.
Housing: Inside city limits, single-family homes from the postwar decades on modest, level lots make up most of the housing. Some tracts replaced the Skyranch airfield, which operated from 1944 to 1951, and apartment buildings supply a smaller share. The surrounding county communities share similar postwar housing, so sales on both sides of the city line often serve as comparables.
Appraisal considerations: City parcels follow La Puente's zoning and ADU rules, while Valinda, West Puente Valley and Bassett follow Los Angeles County's, which matters for second units and SB 9 splits. Houses fronting arterials such as Hacienda Boulevard or Amar Road, and those near industrial uses at the City of Industry boundary, should be compared with similarly exposed sales.
ZIP codes: 91744, 91746

### Walnut (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/walnut)
Named for the Rancho Los Nogales grant and incorporated in 1959, Walnut fills the valley and slopes between the San Jose Hills and the Puente Hills, threaded by city riding and hiking trails. Trustees here often ask about hillside homes, gated-community properties and lots backing to trails.
Housing: Ranch and mid-century homes give way to larger two-story plans from later decades, most on curving streets across the hills and canyons. Snow Creek, around Snow Creek Park in the north, and centrally located Walnut Hills are established single-family areas, while Three Oaks and the guard-gated Terraces at Walnut are newer. Attached housing appears in complexes such as Windwood, and the unincorporated Walnut Islands area to the north holds acreage parcels outside city limits.
Appraisal considerations: Gated communities such as the Terraces at Walnut carry dues, architectural rules and shared amenities, so the analysis leans on sales inside comparable gated settings. Walnut Islands parcels fall within Covina, Pomona and Walnut ZIP codes but follow county zoning for ADUs and lot splits. Lots that meet open space deserve a look at wildfire hazard mapping, and steep ground adds less utility than level usable area.
ZIP codes: 91789

### Diamond Bar (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/diamond-bar)
The diamond-over-a-bar cattle brand of the ranch Transamerica bought in 1956 gave this master-planned city its name; the first homes went up at the north end around 1960, and cityhood followed in 1989. Our work here centers on hillside view homes, properties in The Country Estates and condominiums near the SR-57 and SR-60 junction.
Housing: The north end's early tracts are 1960s ranch houses, and development moved south and up the slopes in later decades as Transamerica and, after it, other developers built curving hillside tracts. The Country Estates is a gated enclave with a staffed entry around the clock, large custom homes on big lots, and a clubhouse, pool and tennis courts. Condominium and townhome complexes, including those around the Diamond Bar Tennis Club area near Golden Springs Drive, supply most attached housing.
Appraisal considerations: Inside The Country Estates, the analysis starts with sales behind the same gates, documenting dues, architectural controls, acreage, view corridors and usable flat area. Wildfire hazard designations should be confirmed for hillside parcels across the city, and any recorded slope or drainage history weighed where it affects marketability. Homes nearest the SR-57 and SR-60 interchange need similarly exposed comparables.
ZIP codes: 91765, 91789

### Hacienda Heights (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/hacienda-heights)
Governed by Los Angeles County rather than a city council, Hacienda Heights lies between the SR-60 and the Puente Hills and was subdivided in 1913 as North Whittier Heights, an orchard district renamed in the early 1960s. Families and attorneys most often bring us long-held 1950s and 1960s houses and hillside view homes.
Housing: Hacienda Boulevard saw the first suburban houses in the 1940s, and 1950s subdivisions near Kwis Avenue spread single-story ranch tracts across the flatter northern ground. In the 1970s, single-family development climbed the northern slopes of the Puente Hills, where split-level and two-story homes gained valley views, and later infill added a few gated projects. Townhomes, condominiums, apartments and mobile home parks make up a smaller share of a predominantly single-family stock.
Appraisal considerations: County zoning and the 2011 Hacienda Heights Community Plan apply, including a hillside management overlay on the steepest slopes that shapes grading, additions and lot splits. The Puente Hills have burned several times, so a hillside parcel's hazard designation and any post-fire market effect deserve attention. Homes near the closed Puente Hills Landfill or along the SR-60 need similarly located comparables.
ZIP codes: 91745

### Rowland Heights (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/rowland-heights)
Stretching from the SR-60 south to the Puente Hills along the Orange County line, Rowland Heights is an unincorporated county community named for John Rowland, who received the Rancho La Puente grant in 1842. Executors often bring hillside homes, gated tract homes, larger agricultural-zoned lots and condominiums.
Housing: Single-story ranch homes from the 1960s and 1970s form much of the older stock, with two-story Spanish-influenced homes in later tracts and on the hillsides. Planned neighborhoods include Rancho El Dorado from the late 1980s and 1990s, the production-built Vantage Pointe tract near Rowland Heights Park, and gated Ridgemoor south of Pathfinder Road. Condominium and townhome pockets sit off Colima Road, while much of the community carries county A-1 light agricultural zoning, and equestrian and agricultural uses persist on larger lots around Desire and Native avenues.
Appraisal considerations: As unincorporated territory, Rowland Heights is subject to the Rowland Heights Community Standards District in the county zoning code, whose standards have been under revision with the East San Gabriel Valley Area Plan, so the version in force on the valuation date matters. Much of the southern hillside area carries a Very High fire hazard rating and lies within the Puente Hills Significant Ecological Area, limiting buildability.
ZIP codes: 91748

### Downey (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/downey)
Downey is one of the larger Gateway cities, set between the Rio Hondo and the San Gabriel River, with an aerospace past and a residential core built mostly after the Second World War. Families and fiduciaries here often need a date-of-death value for a long-held ranch house, a Prop 19 review when a parent's home passes to a child, or a date-of-separation figure in a dissolution.
Housing: Suburban homes replaced farms and orchards after the Second World War, and single-story postwar houses remain common across the city. Lot and house sizes vary noticeably, and some streets mix modest original homes with substantially enlarged or rebuilt houses. Condominiums, townhomes, and apartment buildings add a substantial attached and rental segment.
Appraisal considerations: Homes backing onto the Santa Ana Freeway, the Century Freeway and C Line corridor, or the San Gabriel River Freeway can warrant a location adjustment for noise and traffic. Expanded houses need their permit history compared with the assessor's recorded living area, and blocks near the river channels should be checked against current flood maps. Where a lot carries a rear unit or converted garage, we confirm what is permitted before giving it contributory value.
ZIP codes: 90240, 90241, 90242

### Norwalk (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/norwalk)
Norwalk incorporated in 1957 after its dairies, orchards, and sugar beet fields filled with postwar housing, and it remains a city of single-family neighborhoods with a significant attached-home segment. Trustees and heirs bring us date-of-death and step-up assignments, Prop 19 parent-to-child reviews, and buyout values when siblings decide to keep a family home.
Housing: Postwar single-family houses on modest lots make up much of the stock, and many have been enlarged with later room additions. A few Victorian-era farmhouses survive, the 1891 Hargitt House among them, but they are exceptions. Condominiums, townhomes, apartment complexes, and several mobile home parks add variety, and city housing programs have funded room additions to relieve crowding in larger households.
Appraisal considerations: Parcels beside the Santa Ana, San Gabriel River, or Century freeways, or near the rail corridors, can show measurable external influence, so we choose comparables with similar exposure. Room additions are common and assessor records often lag behind them, so we reconcile the recorded area against photos and permits. A rear unit or converted garage should be documented before it is credited in the value.
ZIP codes: 90650

### Whittier (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/whittier)
Whittier grew from an 1887 Quaker settlement into a city of historic districts, postwar tracts, and hillside neighborhoods at the foot of the Puente Hills, incorporating in 1898. Estate attorneys and trustees here often need retrospective values for older homes with original character, while families working through a divorce or co-owner buyout ask how historic status or a view lot affects value.
Housing: The Central Park, Hadley-Greenleaf, and College Hills historic districts near Uptown Whittier hold many Craftsman and Spanish Colonial Revival homes from the early twentieth century. After the Second World War, orange groves were subdivided into housing tracts, and the city's east side takes in areas such as Friendly Hills, Murphy Ranch, and Leffingwell Ranch. Hillside streets in Friendly Hills and Starlite Estates add sloping lots, some with views, and condominium and townhome complexes add a smaller attached segment.
Appraisal considerations: Homes in the designated historic districts may face review before exterior alterations, which affects both the condition analysis and the pool of comparable sales. Hillside parcels need attention to slope, usable yard area, and view, and older raised-foundation houses should be checked for seismic retrofit work, a lasting concern since the 1987 Whittier Narrows earthquake damaged much of Uptown. Permits for additions on custom homes are worth confirming against the assessor's recorded area.
ZIP codes: 90601, 90602, 90603, 90604, 90605

### South Whittier (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/south-whittier)
South Whittier is an unincorporated community of about five square miles directly south of the City of Whittier, governed by Los Angeles County rather than a city hall. Heirs and trustees settling estates here usually need a date-of-death value for a single-family house, and attorneys often ask how county jurisdiction affects permits, additions, and accessory units.
Housing: The community is predominantly residential, with single-family houses on regular suburban lots forming most of the stock. Later bedroom additions, enclosed patios, and garage conversions are features to verify, and accessory dwelling units have become more common in rear yards. Owner-occupied homes make up a clear majority of the housing.
Appraisal considerations: Permits here run through Los Angeles County rather than a city, so we check county building records and assessor data whenever an addition, patio enclosure, or garage conversion appears in photos. County ADU and SB 9 rules apply to these single-family lots, which can matter when development potential is part of the question. Because addresses carry Whittier mailing names, confirming the parcel's actual jurisdiction is the first step.
ZIP codes: 90604, 90605

### Pico Rivera (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/pico-rivera)
Pico Rivera incorporated in 1958, joining the former farm communities of Pico to the north and Rivera to the south on the plain between the Rio Hondo and the San Gabriel River. Owner-occupied single-family homes predominate, and heirs, trustees, and probate attorneys regularly need date-of-death values, Prop 19 assessments, and buyout figures.
Housing: Builders arrived after the Second World War, and postwar single-family houses make up much of the city's residential area. Additions, patio enclosures, and rear units are common on single-family lots, and owner-occupied homes make up most of the housing. The Ford assembly plant that operated from 1958 to 1980, later used by Northrop, was demolished in 2001, and the Pico Rivera Towne Center now anchors Washington Boulevard.
Appraisal considerations: Pico Rivera sits downstream of Whittier Narrows Dam, which the Army Corps of Engineers said in 2017 no longer met its tolerable-risk guidelines, so we review current FEMA flood-zone status parcel by parcel. Homes near the river levees, the 605, or industrial corridors may need a location adjustment. Rear units and converted garages appear often enough that we confirm permit status before assigning contributory value.
ZIP codes: 90660

### Montebello (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/montebello)
Montebello grew from an 1899 townsite platted beside the railroad and from five-acre farm lots that later filled with houses, and it incorporated in 1920. Its single-family homes and condominiums bring us estate and trust assignments, date-of-separation values for divorcing couples, and gift and Prop 19 transfers within families.
Housing: Blocks near the original townsite include early twentieth-century homes, while postwar tracts cover much of the flatland. Hillside streets in the northern part of the city offer sloping lots and, in places, views. Condominiums, townhomes, and apartments are a significant part of the housing, and renters occupy a majority of units citywide.
Appraisal considerations: Standard Oil's 1917 discovery in the Montebello Hills was followed by decades of drilling, so parcels near former oil operations should be checked against state well records for abandoned wells or setback issues. Hillside homes need analysis of slope, access, and view, and properties along the Pomona or Santa Ana freeways may warrant an external adjustment. Condominium values depend on the project's HOA health as well as the unit itself.
ZIP codes: 90640

### Commerce (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/commerce)
Commerce, incorporated in 1960, is primarily an industrial and distribution city, with a major rail yard, warehouses, and retail along the Santa Ana Freeway and only a modest base of homes. When a family house here passes through an estate or a divorce, the central question is usually how a small home near industry compares with homes in nearby residential communities.
Housing: Housing is concentrated in a few neighborhoods that took shape before incorporation, including Bandini and Rosewood, where residents joined with industrial leaders in the late 1940s to promote the area. The stock combines modest single-family houses with duplexes and small apartment buildings. New residential construction has been limited by the city's industrial land pattern, so the inventory of homes changes slowly.
Appraisal considerations: External obsolescence from rail operations, freight corridors, and the Santa Ana and Long Beach freeways is the central issue, and we measure it with paired sales where possible. Some homes sit next to commercial or industrial zoning, so we confirm the parcel's zoning and whether the residential use is conforming. Limited sales volume often requires an expanded search area and time adjustments, which the report explains.
ZIP codes: 90040, 90022, 90023

### Bell (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/bell)
Bell, named for pioneer James George Bell and incorporated in 1927, is a compact, densely built city along the Los Angeles River between Huntington Park and Bell Gardens. Most households rent, and family-owned lots sometimes carry more than one dwelling, so estate, trust, and partition questions often turn on how to value a parcel with multiple units.
Housing: Population surged between 1920 and the mid-1930s, and many older streets took shape in that period. Later decades added postwar houses, duplexes, and apartment buildings, and some original homes now share their lots with a rear house or added unit. Renters occupy most of the city's housing units, so owner-occupied single-family sales are a smaller share of activity.
Appraisal considerations: For multi-unit lots, we document each structure's permit status and treat unpermitted units cautiously, often reporting their contribution separately. Proximity to the river channel, the Long Beach Freeway, and industrial uses can affect value and is reflected in comparable selection. Retrospective assignments may also call for rent levels from the effective date when income influences what buyers would pay.
ZIP codes: 90201, 90270

### Bell Gardens (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/bell-gardens)
Bell Gardens takes its name from the vegetable farms that covered the area until the 1930s, when inexpensive homes began replacing the fields, and it incorporated in 1961. Today it is a compact, largely renter-occupied city, and owner families bring us date-of-death, trust, and co-owner buyout assignments on small single-family homes and multi-unit lots.
Housing: Builder O.C. Beck began offering low-cost homes in 1930, and Depression-era and wartime construction, much of it for defense-plant workers, left many small houses on modest lots. Most of the housing dates from 1940 through the late 1960s, with apartments and infill units added later, and some single-family lots now hold a second dwelling. The resident-owned Casa Mobile Home Park on Gage Avenue includes the historic Gage Mansion.
Appraisal considerations: Older houses here were often expanded informally over the decades, so we compare the assessor's recorded area with photos and permit records before relying on it. Lots with a rear dwelling require confirmation of legal status. Blocks near the river channels and freeway corridors can carry external influences, which we test with local sales.
ZIP codes: 90201

### Cudahy (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/cudahy)
Cudahy, just over a square mile beside the Los Angeles River, began in 1908 when meatpacker Michael Cudahy subdivided part of Rancho San Antonio into one-acre lots, and it incorporated in 1960. Its unusual parcel pattern shapes almost every valuation here, whether the assignment is a date-of-death value, a trust distribution, or a buyout among siblings.
Housing: The original 'Cudahy lots' were typically 50 to 100 feet wide and 600 to 800 feet deep, intended for gardens, fruit trees, and small livestock. After area factories closed in the late 1970s, many of those deep parcels were redeveloped with stucco apartment complexes, and density rose sharply. Remaining single-family homes vary in age and size, and some sit at the front of a deep lot with additional dwellings behind.
Appraisal considerations: Deep lots can hold value beyond the house itself, but only to the extent zoning, access, and utilities allow further development, so we review the parcel's zoning and any recorded lot splits. Multiple structures on one parcel need to be identified and their permit status confirmed. Highest and best use deserves explicit discussion when a small house sits on an oversized parcel.
ZIP codes: 90201

### Huntington Park (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/huntington-park)
Huntington Park incorporated in 1906 as a streetcar suburb on the Los Angeles Railway, housing workers for the industries southeast of downtown. Its older homes and multi-unit lots generate estate, trust, and divorce valuations in which age, condition, and the number of dwellings on a parcel are central.
Housing: The population grew rapidly during the 1920s, and a notable share of today's homes predate 1940. Postwar and later decades added apartments, duplexes, and rear units, so some single-family parcels now contain more than one dwelling. Condition varies widely, from carefully kept originals to thoroughly remodeled houses.
Appraisal considerations: Older homes may retain original wiring, plumbing, and raised foundations, so condition must be read carefully from the client's photos and any inspection reports. Multi-dwelling parcels need each structure identified, with permitted and unpermitted units distinguished. Homes near rail rights-of-way and industrial frontage along the city's edges can warrant location adjustments.
ZIP codes: 90255

### Maywood (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/maywood)
Maywood is one of the smallest cities in Los Angeles County by area, about 1.2 square miles of tightly built residential streets, and it incorporated in 1924. Families and attorneys here typically need date-of-death, trust, and divorce valuations for small single-family homes, some of which share their lots with a second unit.
Housing: The land was a ranch until 1919, when May Wood lent her name to its subdivision into home tracts, and the residential grid filled in during the following decades. Single-family homes sit on compact lots, reflecting the city's dense street grid. Rear houses, added units, and small apartment buildings appear throughout the city, and renters occupy a large majority of homes.
Appraisal considerations: Where a parcel holds more than one dwelling, unit count and permit history are often decisive, and we report undocumented units separately. On such compact lots, any enlarged house deserves verification of its living area against the assessor's records. Blocks beside industrial uses on the city's edges may call for location adjustments.
ZIP codes: 90270

### South Gate (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/south-gate)
South Gate took its name in 1918 from the South Gate Gardens tract on the former Cudahy Ranch, incorporated in 1923, and grew alongside major plants such as Firestone Tire and Rubber. Heirs and trustees here frequently need values for long-held family homes, and divorce attorneys bring date-of-separation questions on houses that owners have enlarged over time.
Housing: Early developers sold small plots to working families who often built their homes with sweat equity rather than cash, so construction quality and floor plans vary widely from house to house. Between 1910 and 1940 most farmland gave way to homes and factories, and postwar building filled the remaining land. Hollydale lies across the Los Angeles River on the city's east side. Duplexes, rear units, and apartment buildings mix with single-family homes throughout.
Appraisal considerations: Because many homes were owner-built and later enlarged, we compare recorded square footage, photos, and permits closely before settling on living area. Parcels near the river channel, the freeways, and the city's industrial zones may need location adjustments, and flood-zone status should be checked near the levees. Rear units should be identified and their permit status confirmed in every assignment.
ZIP codes: 90280

### Lynwood (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/lynwood)
Lynwood incorporated in 1921 and takes its name from the Lynwood Dairy and Creamery that stood by its Pacific Electric station. The city lies near the junction of the Century and Long Beach freeways, and its single-family homes regularly come to us for date-of-death, trust, and Prop 19 valuations.
Housing: Single-family houses from the interwar and postwar decades line many of the city's residential streets. Additions, converted garages, and rear units are common features to verify. Apartment buildings and other multifamily housing round out the stock.
Appraisal considerations: Homes close to the Century Freeway corridor can be affected by noise and visual impact, so street-level location matters. We verify added living area and any rear units against permits and the assessor's record. Proximity to the Long Beach Freeway and to industrial uses along its corridor may call for location adjustments.
ZIP codes: 90262

### Compton (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/compton)
Compton, incorporated in 1888, is one of the oldest cities in Los Angeles County and sits within a ring formed by the 105, 110, 710, and 91 freeways. It has a large base of owner-occupied single-family homes, and families here frequently need date-of-death values, trust and estate support, and Prop 19 reviews for long-held family homes.
Housing: Single-family houses make up much of the city, and many streets still have the spacious homes that once made Compton a sought-after suburb. Richland Farms, set aside under Griffith D. Compton's original land donation, keeps large residential lots where livestock and gardens are permitted. Sunny Cove and Leland are distinct residential areas, and additions and rear units appear across the city.
Appraisal considerations: Richland Farms parcels require attention to their agricultural zoning, barns and animal structures, and the limited pool of truly similar sales. Homes near the airport, the Alameda Corridor, or the freeways may need location adjustments. We confirm the permit status of rear units and garage conversions before including them in living area or unit count.
ZIP codes: 90220, 90221, 90222

### Paramount (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/paramount)
Paramount was created in 1948 when the communities of Hynes and Clearwater merged their post offices, and it incorporated in 1957 to avoid annexation by its neighbors. Once a regional hay and dairy market, it is now a compact city of homes and industry, and its families ask us for estate, trust, divorce, and Prop 19 valuations.
Housing: Single-family houses on modest lots make up much of the residential area, and many have been enlarged over time. Apartments, townhomes, and condominiums add a large attached and rental segment. Renters occupy a majority of the city's homes, so owner-occupied single-family sales are a smaller slice of activity.
Appraisal considerations: Blocks next to industrial operations may carry external obsolescence, and we test that with sales rather than assuming it. The Long Beach Freeway along the western border and the Century Freeway to the north affect nearby homes. Additions and converted garages should be verified against permits and county records.
ZIP codes: 90723

### Bellflower (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/bellflower)
Bellflower began as Somerset in the early 1900s, served as a dairy center, and incorporated in 1957 as farmland gave way to subdivisions for the region's growing workforce. Heirs, trustees, and family-law attorneys bring us date-of-death, step-up, and date-of-separation assignments on its single-family homes and condominiums.
Housing: After the Second World War, rising land values pushed dairy operations east toward the area that became Cerritos, and the former farms were subdivided into housing tracts. Bellflower Boulevard, a busy shopping strip from the 1950s through the late 1960s, remains the city's main thoroughfare. Apartments, townhomes, and condominiums make up a large part of the housing, and renters occupy most units.
Appraisal considerations: Homes along the Artesia Freeway or near the San Gabriel River corridor may warrant location adjustments, and parcels next to the future rail line deserve a note on potential change. Older lots sometimes carry a second dwelling, so we confirm permits and unit count. For condominium units, we review HOA information supplied by the client along with sales in the same or similar projects.
ZIP codes: 90706

### Lakewood (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/lakewood)
Lakewood is the planned postwar suburb whose Lakewood Park tract produced about 17,500 houses between 1950 and 1953, and the city pioneered the contract-services 'Lakewood Plan' when it incorporated in 1954. Its owner-occupied neighborhoods produce a steady flow of date-of-death values, IRS step-up figures, and Prop 19 parent-to-child reviews.
Housing: The Lakewood Park Corporation, formed by Louis Boyar, Mark Taper, and Ben Weingart, built one-story two- and three-bedroom houses designed by architect Paul Duncan, roughly 825 to 1,050 square feet as sold, in dozens of exterior variations. Other named tracts include Mayfair, the Lakewood Mutuals, Carson Park, and Lakewood Gardens, while the Lakewood Country Club Estates area holds homes built from the mid-1930s to 1960. Neighborhoods east of the San Gabriel River came in the late 1950s and early 1960s, Pennswood Square introduced two-story homes in 1965, and Westgate followed in the 1990s.
Appraisal considerations: Matching the original floor plan shows how much living area has been added, and many houses have grown through room additions over the decades, so permits and the assessor's record should agree with the photos. Homes along Lakewood, Bellflower, and Del Amo boulevards or near the 605 may need location adjustments. Westgate, built on a former oil transfer facility, and the eastern annexation areas should be compared within their own tracts.
ZIP codes: 90712, 90713, 90715

### Cerritos (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/cerritos)
Cerritos incorporated in 1956 as Dairy Valley, a city of hundreds of dairies, then voted in 1963 to open the land to residential building and took its current name in 1967. Its single-family tracts and townhome communities, largely built within about a decade, bring estate, trust, Prop 19, and divorce assignments where tract and model matching is central.
Housing: Most houses date from the late 1960s and 1970s, when Cerritos was the fastest-growing city in California, and most were built as planned tract subdivisions. Owner-occupied single-family homes predominate, joined by townhome and condominium communities governed by homeowners associations. Many original houses have since been expanded or remodeled, which widens the spread within a single tract.
Appraisal considerations: Because many homes share original plans, we identify the model and measure additions against it, confirming permits for any expansion. Townhome and condominium values require review of HOA dues, reserves, and any special assessments, and units near the 605 or 91 may warrant a location adjustment. Comparing sales across different tracts without adjustment can mislead, since builders and plans differ.
ZIP codes: 90703

### Artesia (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/artesia)
Artesia, named for the artesian wells that once watered its farms, is a city of about 1.6 square miles that incorporated in 1959 and is bordered by Cerritos on three sides. Its single-family homes and townhomes come to us for estate settlements, trust administration, and family transfers under Prop 19.
Housing: After the Second World War, developers pressed to replace the area's dairies with residential tracts, and much of the city's housing dates from the postwar decades. Townhomes, condominiums, and apartments add density. Some homes have been enlarged or rebuilt, so house sizes can vary on the same street.
Appraisal considerations: With the city so small, we often include Cerritos and Norwalk sales and adjust for location where the market shows a difference. Homes near the Artesia Freeway or backing onto Pioneer Boulevard commercial lots may need location adjustments. Rebuilt and expanded houses require careful verification of living area against permits and county records.
ZIP codes: 90701

### Hawaiian Gardens (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/hawaiian-gardens)
Hawaiian Gardens covers less than a square mile at the county's southeastern edge and takes its name from a palm-decorated fruit stand that opened at Carson Street and Norwalk Boulevard in 1927. It incorporated in 1964, largely to avoid annexation by Long Beach, and its families bring us estate, trust, and partition-related valuations on small homes and multi-unit lots.
Housing: Before incorporation the area, known as The Delta, was rural, and Depression-era buyers built or bought modest homes despite unpaved roads and frequent flooding, including a major flood in 1952. Road paving was not completed until 1968. Today small single-family houses mix with apartments, and rental housing makes up a large part of the stock.
Appraisal considerations: Given the area's flooding history, we check current FEMA flood-zone status, and older homes from the Depression era warrant close review of construction quality and permits. Parcels with rear units or added dwellings need each unit's legal status confirmed. Homes adjacent to commercial lots or casino traffic may warrant a location adjustment.
ZIP codes: 90716

### La Mirada (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/la-mirada)
La Mirada was developed on ranch land once owned by Chicago mapmaker Andrew McNally, whose Windermere Ranch was surrounded by olive, orange, and lemon groves, and it was promoted in the early 1950s as a completely planned city before incorporating in 1960. Its owner-occupied neighborhoods produce estate, trust, and Prop 19 assignments as well as divorce valuations for single-family homes and townhomes.
Housing: In 1954 developer Louis M. Halper bought most of the land, planned roughly 10,000 homes, and sold parcels to other builders under a civic council that oversaw quality. Tracts of three- and four-bedroom houses went up quickly, and the city counted more than 8,000 homes by 1960. Townhome and condominium communities governed by homeowners associations add attached options.
Appraisal considerations: Homes near the Santa Ana Freeway, which crosses the city's southwest corner, may warrant a location adjustment. Because builders sold tracts with standard plans, identifying the original model helps measure additions, and we check permits for expanded living area. For townhomes, we review HOA dues, reserves, and any litigation or special assessments disclosed in documents the client provides.
ZIP codes: 90638

### Santa Fe Springs (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/santa-fe-springs)
Santa Fe Springs, incorporated in 1957, is dominated by industry and distribution, the legacy of an oil rush that followed the Union-Bell gusher of 1921, and it has a comparatively small base of homes. When a house here is part of an estate, trust, or divorce, the key questions are usually how industrial surroundings, oil-field history, and the limited number of local sales affect value.
Housing: Residential neighborhoods occupy a limited share of the city's nearly nine square miles, mostly single-family houses, along with planned developments such as The Villages at Heritage Springs. Owner-occupied homes make up the majority of the housing. Some neighborhoods border industrial parks directly, and older homes may sit near former oil-production land.
Appraisal considerations: Oil drilling here dates to 1907, so parcels on or near former well sites should be checked against state well records, and any disclosed methane mitigation or plugged wells noted. Industrial adjacency and truck routes create external influences that vary block by block. Limited local sales often require an expanded search with clear support for location adjustments.
ZIP codes: 90670, 90605

### Torrance (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/torrance)
Torrance spans much of the South Bay, from its own stretch of Santa Monica Bay beachfront inland past Del Amo Fashion Center toward the Harbor Freeway. Because the city is so large, heirs and trustees holding a long-owned tract house, a Riviera hillside home or a townhome usually want to know first how much its particular location matters.
Housing: Old Torrance, the 1912 townsite designed by the Olmsted Brothers, keeps Craftsman houses and bungalows on Gramercy and Andreo avenues near El Prado Park. Most of the city filled in after World War II, when tracts such as Southwood and Seaside Ranchos spread one-story ranch houses across ordinary suburban lots. The Hollywood Riviera climbs hillside streets above Torrance Beach, Walteria sits below the Palos Verdes hills, and townhomes of several vintages appear citywide.
Appraisal considerations: Riviera view homes are graded on outlook and slope first, using sales from the same hillside streets. Exposure to the PBF Energy refinery, Zamperini Field and the busiest arterials is weighed block by block, and because many Southwood and Seaside houses have been enlarged, permits and recorded living area are reconciled with the family's photos.
ZIP codes: 90501, 90502, 90503, 90504, 90505

### Redondo Beach (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/redondo-beach)
Redondo Beach wraps around King Harbor and its pier at the south end of Santa Monica Bay, with North Redondo reaching inland and South Redondo following the sand to Riviera Village. Many estate files involve long-held houses near the beach, North Redondo townhomes or older homes whose worth lies mostly in the land beneath them.
Housing: South Redondo mixes early beach cottages, period houses and modern rebuilds on the lettered avenues, which run inland from the Esplanade and its bluff-top condominium buildings. North Redondo was largely built after World War II with one-story houses, many later replaced by pairs of attached or detached townhomes known locally as two-on-a-lots. Golden Hills is a hillside enclave of homes oriented toward views.
Appraisal considerations: A two-on-a-lot unit may be a condominium sharing land with its twin or a separate fee parcel, and the recorded map decides which comparables apply. Esplanade condominiums are compared within the same buildings, confirming dues, assessments and view direction. Redondo has contested SB 9 lot-split rules, so any development premium on an older lot must come from sales that actually paid one.
ZIP codes: 90277, 90278

### Hermosa Beach (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/hermosa-beach)
Hermosa Beach is a small, densely built city between Manhattan Beach and Redondo Beach, organized around Pier Avenue, Pier Plaza and the Strand. Older cottages, side-by-side condominiums and Strand frontage come up often in trust and estate work here, where land value, views and distance from the sand drive most of the discussion.
Housing: A few 1920s cottages survive, but much of the Sand Section has been rebuilt with multi-level modern homes and two-unit condominiums on narrow lots. Walk streets west of Hermosa Avenue trade car frontage for landscaped pedestrian paths, and many of the sloped ones face the ocean. From the Hermosa Valley Greenbelt, the Valley Section climbs hilly streets toward Pacific Coast Highway, and the Hill Section on the far side of the highway mixes houses, townhomes and view condominiums.
Appraisal considerations: Older Sand Section cottages often sell for their site value, so land sales and a highest-and-best-use analysis sit alongside improved comparables. Two-unit condominiums are matched with similar projects, noting shared walls and any maintenance agreement, and for walk-street and Strand homes, paired sales from the same block band isolate the frontage premium.
ZIP codes: 90254

### Manhattan Beach (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/manhattan-beach)
Manhattan Beach runs along about two miles of shoreline between El Segundo and Hermosa Beach, with the Sand, Hill and Tree sections west of Sepulveda Boulevard and a broad eastside of mid-century neighborhoods beyond it. When an executor inherits an original house here, the land usually carries most of the value, and the central question becomes how much the older structure still contributes.
Housing: The dunes were graded away in the 1920s and 1930s, and custom homes have replaced most early cottages. The Tree Section has larger interior lots, the Hill Section has view homes on its slopes, and El Porto is known for half lots. East of Sepulveda, mid-century houses in Manhattan Heights and Liberty Village are steadily being rebuilt, the Poets Section has larger lots, and gated Manhattan Village mixes court homes, townhomes and estate homes.
Appraisal considerations: Because many buyers are paying for the lot, land and teardown purchases are analyzed beside improved sales to show what the existing house adds. Since 2010 new homes may not span more than two lots, which caps any assemblage premium, and in El Porto, half-lot homes and the neighboring Chevron refinery are handled with comparables from the same blocks.
ZIP codes: 90266

### El Segundo (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/el-segundo)
El Segundo grew up around the Standard Oil refinery that opened in 1911, and its housing is concentrated in the northwest part of the city, between Los Angeles International Airport and the refinery grounds. Probate and trust assignments typically concern modest older houses near Main Street, and airport noise, rebuilding activity and tight supply come up repeatedly.
Housing: Early bungalows and Spanish-style cottages remain around downtown, and one-story postwar houses fill much of the rest of the grid. Lots are modest, two-family parcels are scattered throughout, and steady rebuilding has added larger two-story homes. Apartments and condominiums cluster near downtown, and Smoky Hollow, long a light-industrial district, is opening to mixed-use housing under its specific plan.
Appraisal considerations: Thousands of homes here received airport-funded sound insulation such as dual-pane windows, solid-core doors and attic treatment; documented work is credited within condition rather than as a separate premium. Position relative to Imperial Avenue and the refinery edge is weighed with sales from the same part of the grid, and thin inventory can justify a longer search period before reaching into Manhattan Beach or Westchester.
ZIP codes: 90245

### Hawthorne (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/hawthorne)
Hawthorne lies southeast of LAX along the Century and San Diego freeways, and its story runs from Northrop's aircraft plants to the SpaceX headquarters beside Hawthorne Municipal Airport. Divorce and estate matters typically involve modest houses, condominiums or townhomes, and many turn on which side of the 405 the property sits.
Housing: Much of the city was built out in the decades after World War II with one-story stucco houses on standard lots, and apartment buildings make up a large share of the housing. West of the 405, Hollyglen is largely 1950s houses built from a few floor plans, plus some 1980s homes and newer townhome communities such as Three Sixty South Bay. Holly Park, Moneta Gardens and Bodger Park are other established residential areas.
Appraisal considerations: Del Aire, an unincorporated area Hawthorne surrounds on three sides, includes homes with Hawthorne addresses, so jurisdiction is confirmed from the assessor record first. Garage conversions and room additions are common in the postwar tracts and are checked against permits, and freeway or airport noise is handled with sales at similar distances from the source.
ZIP codes: 90250

### Lawndale (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/lawndale)
Lawndale is a compact city strung along Hawthorne Boulevard between Hawthorne, Redondo Beach, Torrance and the unincorporated Alondra Park area. Added rear units, permit gaps and the use of sales from neighboring cities come up most often with the modest houses and small townhomes typical of estate files here.
Housing: Charles Hopper founded the town in 1905, and the Lawndale Acres subdivisions that followed sold modest parcels suited to small-scale farming. The heaviest building came after World War II, when returning veterans created demand for small one-story houses, and homes from the 1940s and 1950s still dominate the stock. Later decades replaced some older houses with apartments and small townhome projects, and some lots pair a front house with a second dwelling behind it.
Appraisal considerations: Rear units are common enough that permit status is checked before any contribution is credited, and unpermitted space is described but weighed cautiously. With relatively few monthly sales, comparables often come from adjoining North Redondo, Hawthorne, Torrance and Alondra Park blocks, with location differences supported by paired data.
ZIP codes: 90260

### Gardena (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/gardena)
Gardena sits in the middle of the South Bay between Hawthorne, Torrance and the Harbor Gateway strip of Los Angeles, close to the 405, 110 and 91 freeways. Once known for strawberry fields, it now holds postwar houses, condominiums and townhomes, and estate questions often arise when a Gardena address does not match the actual jurisdiction.
Housing: Gardena began as an 1887 subdivision and spent its early decades in berry fields and truck farms, absorbing the neighboring Moneta settlement when the city incorporated in 1930. Most housing arrived after World War II as tracts of one-story stucco houses on standard lots, followed by apartments and condominium complexes in later decades. The ground is flat throughout, and Hollypark and Strawberry Park remain common neighborhood references.
Appraisal considerations: Gardena ZIP codes also serve parts of Harbor Gateway in the City of Los Angeles and several unincorporated county pockets, so the governing jurisdiction is established before any permit research. Condominium files call for dues, special assessments and any pending project litigation at the date of value, and additions in the postwar tracts are reconciled with permits and assessor square footage.
ZIP codes: 90247, 90248, 90249

### Inglewood (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/inglewood)
Immediately east of LAX, Inglewood combines level blocks near the airport with rolling terrain in several of its neighborhoods. The former Hollywood Park racetrack now holds SoFi Stadium and its surrounding district, so many retrospective assignments turn on whether the effective date falls before or after that change, along with airport noise and older-home condition.
Housing: Spanish Revival houses and period bungalows from the 1920s and 1930s are common in the older neighborhoods. Morningside Park and Fairview Heights mix period and postwar homes, and Inglewood Knolls is a tract completed in 1953–54. Apartments make up a large share of the housing, and condominium complexes, including gated communities near Morningside Park, appear across the city.
Appraisal considerations: Homes under LAX approach paths may have been insulated through the city's long-running sound program, and verified improvements are reflected in the condition rating. When the effective date falls during the stadium's announcement or construction, same-period sales carry the most weight, and since unrecorded additions are common in older homes, living area is reconciled with permits and client photos.
ZIP codes: 90301, 90302, 90303, 90305

### Carson (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/carson)
Carson spreads across the flatlands north of Wilmington and the Port of Los Angeles, with California State University, Dominguez Hills and Dignity Health Sports Park in its northern half. Incorporated in 1968, it produces estate and family-law files involving long-held tract houses, condominiums and homes near refineries or industrial land.
Housing: Most single-family homes went up in the postwar decades as one- and two-story tracts on largely level ground. Condominium complexes and numerous mobile home parks add to the mix. Some tracts sit on or beside former oil and industrial land, most notably the Carousel Tract, built on a former oil storage site and placed under a state cleanup order in 2011.
Appraisal considerations: Environmental history belongs in the record: refinery operations, the Carousel Tract cleanup and the fall 2021 Dominguez Channel odor episode are noted as they stood on the effective date, without environmental conclusions. Mobile homes on leased park spaces fall outside our scope, and because ZIP 90810 overlaps West Long Beach, jurisdiction is verified before comparables are chosen.
ZIP codes: 90745, 90746, 90810

### Lomita (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/lomita)
Lomita covers less than two square miles between Torrance, the Los Angeles community of Harbor City and the Palos Verdes Peninsula, with Narbonne Avenue and Pacific Coast Highway as its main streets. Finding enough local comparables is the recurring challenge in so small a market, whether the property is a modest house, a condominium or a small townhome.
Housing: The town began in 1907 as a settlement on a seven-square-mile tract, much of which Torrance annexed in the 1950s. What remains is flat to gently rising ground lined with small one-story postwar houses, many on land that once grew vegetables when Lomita called itself the celery capital. Residents incorporated in 1964 partly to head off high-rise apartments, and today apartments, condominiums and small townhome projects sit among houses on many blocks.
Appraisal considerations: Blocks nearest Zamperini Field's traffic pattern and the commercial corridors are compared with similarly placed homes. Rear units, patio enclosures and garage conversions are checked against permit history before any of that space is counted, and condominium dues, reserves and special assessments are documented for the date of value.
ZIP codes: 90717

### Palos Verdes Estates (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/palos-verdes-estates)
Palos Verdes Estates occupies the northwest corner of the Palos Verdes Peninsula, where a 1923 planned community laid out by Frederick Law Olmsted Jr. and Charles Cheney became a city in 1939. Trustees here typically handle substantial single-family homes, where view quality, architectural restrictions and the scarcity of truly similar custom houses shape the analysis.
Housing: About half the land was set aside for roads, parks and open space, and new construction still goes through the Palos Verdes Homes Association's Art Jury. Malaga Cove holds much of the early Mediterranean-style housing on terraced hillsides, and Valmonte mixes period revival and ranch houses under mature trees. Lunada Bay's lower streets run near the bluffs with Margate rising behind, Montemalaga has the newest homes, and the few condominiums sit near the commercial plazas.
Appraisal considerations: Art Jury history matters: an addition that skipped review is described as such, and a realistic rebuild depends on what the Homes Association would approve. View quality is graded on angle, breadth and permanence against sales with similar outlooks, and bluff-top or steep lots call for any geology reports the family can provide.
ZIP codes: 90274

### Rancho Palos Verdes (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/rancho-palos-verdes)
Rancho Palos Verdes covers the southern and eastern slopes of the Palos Verdes Peninsula, from Miraleste above the harbor to the ocean bluffs at Point Vicente and Portuguese Bend. A mostly single-family city incorporated in 1973, it brings estate questions centered on views, geologic hazards and the active landslide complex.
Housing: Much of the housing dates from the 1950s through the 1970s, with ranch and contemporary homes stepping down hillsides toward the water. Miraleste lots are larger but often steep, west-side tracts such as Lunada Pointe hold newer and larger homes, and townhomes concentrate in the Crest area and along Palos Verdes Drive South. Many Eastview streets carry San Pedro addresses.
Appraisal considerations: The Greater Portuguese Bend–Ancient Altamira landslide complex nearly doubled in active area by 2024, bringing red and yellow tags, utility shutoffs and emergency declarations to Seaview, the Portuguese Bend Beach Club and the Portuguese Bend Community Association, and later a FEMA-funded voluntary buyout program. Values must reflect tag status, utility service and landslide-moratorium limits in force on the effective date, with sales inside the complex examined individually.
ZIP codes: 90275

### Rolling Hills Estates (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/rolling-hills-estates)
Covering the northern slopes of the Palos Verdes Peninsula around Peninsula Center and the Promenade on the Peninsula, Rolling Hills Estates has kept a horse-country character since incorporating in 1957. Valuation work here usually involves ranch-style homes on large lots, condominiums near the commercial center and, since 2023, canyon-edge geology.
Housing: Many homes are single-story ranch designs on generous lots, with horse-keeping zoning, corrals and bridle-trail access in neighborhoods such as Dapplegray, Empty Saddle and Rollingwood. Later tracts brought larger two-story homes, some behind gates. Attached housing is concentrated around Peninsula Center and the Crest area, from older condominium complexes to newer buildings on Deep Valley Drive.
Appraisal considerations: The 2023 Peartree Lane landslide destroyed homes along a canyon rim, so canyon-edge parcels call for a check of hazard status and any repair or monitoring history at the date of value. The shared Palos Verdes Peninsula mailing name blurs lines with unincorporated pockets and the separate gated City of Rolling Hills, so we confirm which city, if any, governs the parcel, and barns and arenas count only to the degree buyers pay for them.
ZIP codes: 90274, 90275

### Long Beach (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/long-beach)
Long Beach is the county's second-largest city, reaching from its downtown waterfront and the Port of Long Beach north past the 405 and east to Alamitos Bay and the Orange County line. Its housing range is unusually wide, so trustees and attorneys bring everything from downtown high-rise condominiums to historic-district bungalows, Naples canal homes and postwar tracts.
Housing: Early twentieth-century Craftsman, bungalow and Spanish Revival homes fill Belmont Heights and the locally designated Bluff Park and California Heights historic districts. Naples, begun in 1905 on three islands in Alamitos Bay, has canal-front houses behind concrete seawalls. Los Altos and other east-side areas filled in after World War II with ranch houses, North Long Beach and the West Side hold many smaller homes, and downtown adds towers and lofts.
Appraisal considerations: Historic district homes need a Certificate of Appropriateness for exterior changes, and some carry Mills Act contracts that pass to the next owner. Downtown and coastal condominium files call for dues, reserves, assessments and any balcony inspection findings, and Naples homes are compared on seawall condition and frontage within the same island and canal.
ZIP codes: 90802, 90803, 90804, 90805, 90806, 90807, 90808, 90810, 90813, 90814, 90815

### Belmont Shore (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/belmont-shore)
Belmont Shore is a flat, closely built beach neighborhood in southeast Long Beach, organized around the Second Street shopping district between the Ocean Boulevard sand and Alamitos Bay. Most assignments involve houses or condominiums within a few blocks of the water, where block position, parking and any unit behind the main house drive the analysis.
Housing: Building took off in the 1920s and 1930s, when Spanish Revival and cottage-style homes filled the grid; many have since been remodeled or replaced by larger modern houses, and small apartment and condominium buildings share many blocks. Lots are narrow, often with rear-alley garages, some topped by a second dwelling. Ocean Boulevard homes face the sand behind a late-1930s retaining wall.
Appraisal considerations: A house with a permitted accessory unit stays within a single-family assignment, but a legal duplex does not, so the unit count is settled at intake. Flood-zone designation near Alamitos Bay and the adjoining Peninsula is confirmed for the date of value, and comparables are drawn from the same location band, since a few blocks of distance from the sand can outweigh differences in house size.
ZIP codes: 90803

### Bixby Knolls (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/bixby-knolls)
Bixby Knolls is a residential district in north-central Long Beach between the 405 and Del Amo Boulevard, on land once part of the Bixby family's Rancho Los Cerritos holdings. Its custom period homes, the Virginia Country Club enclave and the Atlantic Avenue business strip bring frequent estate and date-of-death assignments, many involving architecturally distinctive houses.
Housing: Custom homes from the interwar years make up much of the neighborhood, in Spanish Colonial Revival, Tudor Revival, Craftsman and other period styles, with occasional modernist designs. Los Cerritos, around Virginia Country Club, holds estate-sized homes, including work by Kirtland Cutter and by Greene and Greene, and La Linda Drive forms one of its gated sections. Some originals have been replaced with larger houses.
Appraisal considerations: Architect-designed and historically significant homes are matched on quality and design rather than square footage alone, and the architect is named when records confirm it. Because estate-level sales near the country club are infrequent, the report states how far back and how wide the search went, and proximity to Long Beach Airport, the 405 and Atlantic Avenue frontage is weighed with sales in similar positions.
ZIP codes: 90807

### Signal Hill (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/signal-hill)
Signal Hill is a small city completely surrounded by Long Beach, rising about 365 feet to a summit with views from downtown Los Angeles to Catalina. Its 1921 oil strike crowded the hill with derricks, and today's questions often concern view homes and townhomes built on that former oil land and how nearby wells affect value.
Housing: A small historic district near the Heritage Square site preserves some of the city's older houses. As production wound down, parts of the hill were redeveloped with view homes and with townhome and condominium complexes run by their own associations. Upper streets are steep, and remaining housing sites such as Walnut Bluff and Orange Bluff sit on former oil land that must be remediated before construction.
Appraisal considerations: Producing, idle and abandoned wells remain scattered through the city, so well locations from state records and any city oil and gas code requirements are noted, without engineering conclusions. View quality is documented with client photos, and because Signal Hill used Long Beach ZIP codes until 2002, older records may show a Long Beach ZIP.
ZIP codes: 90755

### San Pedro (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/san-pedro)
San Pedro is the City of Los Angeles community at the south end of the Harbor Freeway, between the Port of Los Angeles and Rancho Palos Verdes, with Pacific frontage at Point Fermin and White Point. Estate files range from century-old homes near downtown to hillside view houses and condominiums, and questions center on views, bluff stability and port proximity.
Housing: Victorian, Craftsman and early bungalow homes cluster near downtown, including the Vinegar Hill Historic Preservation Overlay Zone. Postwar ranch tracts climb the hills toward the Palos Verdes border, many oriented to ocean, harbor or Catalina views, with South Shores holding a concentration of them. Condominiums and townhomes are common near downtown and along the Western Avenue and Gaffey Street corridors.
Appraisal considerations: The bluffs have a record of movement, from the 1929 slide that created Sunken City at Point Fermin to the 2011 collapse of Paseo del Mar near White Point, so bluff-side parcels warrant a check of mapped hazard zones and geology reports. Vinegar Hill HPOZ homes need city design review for exterior changes, and permits are verified with the City of Los Angeles.
ZIP codes: 90731, 90732

### Wilmington (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/wilmington)
Phineas Banning developed Wilmington as the original Los Angeles harbor town in the late 1850s; the City of Los Angeles annexed it in 1909, and port terminals, refineries and the Wilmington oil field now surround it. Assignments usually involve modest older houses on small lots, and industrial proximity, added units and permit history are the recurring questions.
Housing: Older blocks near Avalon Boulevard and Banning Park include early twentieth-century bungalows and cottages. One-story postwar houses cover much of the rest, on modest lots that sometimes carry a second dwelling or later additions. Apartment buildings mix with single-family streets, and the housing changes noticeably where neighborhoods meet industrial land.
Appraisal considerations: Industrial and oil-field adjacency, including active drill sites, refinery operations and port truck routes, is documented for the effective date and gauged against sales with comparable exposure. Rear units and additions are checked against Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety records before counting as living area, and because many older houses have seen limited updating, condition ratings lean heavily on client photos.
ZIP codes: 90744

### Avalon (Catalina Island) (https://lavaluepro.com/areas/avalon)
Avalon, the only incorporated city on Santa Catalina Island, sits a little over an hour by ferry from Long Beach, San Pedro and Dana Point and forms a self-contained housing market. For a cottage, hillside home or second-home condominium alike, the central question is how to find adequate comparables when every sale must come from the island.
Housing: Avalon's homes fill a narrow valley opening onto the bay, with small cottages on the flat blocks inland from Crescent Avenue and houses stepping up the slopes and into Avalon Canyon. Hamilton Cove, a gated condominium enclave on the shoreline northwest of town, is largely owned as vacation property. Because materials arrive by barge, building and remodeling cost more than on the mainland.
Appraisal considerations: Comparables come from Avalon itself, since mainland sales do not reflect island access, freight costs or utility constraints, and the search period is widened as needed with market-condition adjustments. Golf carts and city vehicle permits are not real property and are excluded from the value, and Hamilton Cove units are compared within the complex first, with dues confirmed.
ZIP codes: 90704
